三月十九日
translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors
On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing (1559), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. His Majesty took his place at the Dachao Gate and personally bestowed the policy question.
On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, the civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard arranged the imperial ceremonial regalia within the vermilion court. His Majesty took his place at the Dachao Gate. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites reverently carried the yellow proclamation of results, led by drums and music, out beyond the Chang’an Left Gate, where it was posted. Once this was done, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.
On the nineteenth day of the third month…

punctuated:
賜宴於禮部，宴畢赴鴻臚寺習儀。
三月二十一日，賜狀元朝服冠帶及進士寶鈔。
三月二十二日，狀元率諸進士上表謝恩。
三月二十三日，狀元率諸進士詣先師孔子廟行釋菜禮。
禮部奏請，命工部於國子監立石題名。
translation_en:
…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, they went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the first-place graduate was granted court robes, a cap, and a belt, and the metropolitan graduates were granted paper currency.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite.
The Ministry of Rites memorialized to request that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe their names upon it.

福建鄉試第五十五名 會試第七十二名
punctuated:
第一甲三名，賜進士及第。

丁士美〔貫直隸淮安府清河縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字邦彦，行一，年三十九，三月初七日生〕。曾祖進，祖鳳，父儒，母仲氏。嚴侍下，弟士良，娶周氏，繼娶李氏。應天府鄉試第十九名，會試第二百六十七名。

毛惇元〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字裕仁，行十一，年三十五，四月初五日生〕。曾祖傑〔進士，贈刑部主事〕，祖憲〔按察司副使〕，父文炳〔順天府治中〕，母周氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，兄紹元〔布政司參政〕、茂元、坤元、景元、宗元、完元、贊元，弟翼元〔進士〕、萬元〔監生〕，娶楊氏。浙江鄉試第三十七名，會試第三名。

林士章〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字德斐，行七，年三十六，十一月三十日生〕。曾祖敦碩，祖竦，父烽，母蔡氏。具慶下，兄德華、楚〔貢士〕、德憲、德燦、德喬、德標，弟德師、坫、壎，娶柳氏。福建鄉試第五十五名，會試第七十二名。
translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the degree of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Ding Shimei was registered in a civilian household in Qinghe County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bangyan, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-nine years old, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Feng, his father Ru, and his mother née Zhong. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Shiliang. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Dunyuan was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuren, and he ranked eleventh among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jie was a metropolitan graduate, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather Xian was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his father Wenbing was Administrative Assistant of Shuntian Prefecture. His mother, née Zhou, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shaoyuan, an Administration Vice Commissioner, Maoyuan, Kunyuan, Jingyuan, Zongyuan, Wanyuan (完元), and Zanyuan. His younger brothers were Yiyuan, a metropolitan graduate, and Wanyuan (萬元), an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shizhang was registered in a military household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Defei, and he ranked seventh among his brothers. He was thirty-six years old, born on the thirtieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dunshuo, his grandfather Song, his father Feng, and his mother née Cai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dehua, Chu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Dexian, Decan, Deqiao, and Debiao; his younger brothers were Deshi, Dian, and Xun. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖玉 祖完 父濂〔副千戶〕 前母郭氏 母晉氏 繼母侯氏
具慶下 弟子頴〔百戶〕 娶杜氏

punctuated:
第二甲八十五名，賜進士出身。

陸光祚〔貫錦衣衛官籍，浙江嘉興府平湖縣人，國子生，治書經，字與培，行三，年三十一，五月初七日生〕。曾祖鋹〔知縣，累贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖淞〔南京光祿寺卿，贈都察院右副都御史〕，父槩，母張氏。永感下。兄〔光祖，工部尚書〕、光泰〔前南京禮部郎中〕、光裕〔貢士〕，弟光儒、光倫〔錦衣衛指揮使〕、光弼〔監生〕、光晉〔錦衣衛指揮使〕、光載〔金吾右衛正千戶〕。娶王氏。順天府鄉試第三名，會試第二百四十三名。

何子壽〔貫錦衣衛衣中所官籍，國子生，治春秋，字康伯，行一，年三十二，十月初十日生〕。曾祖玉，祖完，父濂〔副千戶〕，前母郭氏，母查氏，繼母任氏。具慶下。弟子穎〔百戶〕。娶杜氏。順天府鄉試第十名，會試第一百七十四名。

王湜〔貫江西南昌府新建縣民籍，浙江台州府臨海縣人，縣學附學生，治詩經，字定甫，行三，年三十一，九月初十日生〕。曾祖允壽〔儀賓，贈中大夫〕，祖朝卿〔進士〕，父諫〔府通判〕，母康氏，繼母徐氏。永感下。兄淑〔同科進士〕，弟澍。娶陳氏。江西鄉試第八十五名，會試第二百二十名。
translation_en:
Second class: eighty-five men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Lu Guangzuo, courtesy name Yupei, was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Chang was a county magistrate, posthumously granted successive honors culminating in Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather Song was Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in Nanjing, posthumously honored as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Gai, and his mother was née Zhang; his parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guangzu, Minister of Works; Guangtai, formerly a bureau director in the Ministry of Rites in Nanjing; and Guangyu, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Guangru; Guanglun, commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; Guangbi, an Imperial University student; Guangjin, commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; and Guangzai, battalion commander of the Right Jinwu Guard. His wife was née Wang. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Zishou, courtesy name Kangbo, was registered in an officer household of the “Yizhong Battalion” [?] of the Embroidered Uniform Guard. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather was Wan, and his father was Lian, a vice battalion commander. His father's former wife was née Guo, his mother was née Zha, and his stepmother was née Ren; both parents were living. His younger brother Ziying was a company commander. His wife was née Du. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shi, courtesy name Dingfu, was registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a native of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Yunshou was a ceremonial escort, posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Palace; his grandfather Chaoqing was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); and his father Jian was an assistant prefect. His mother was née Kang, and his stepmother was née Xu; his parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother Shu 淑 earned metropolitan graduate status in the same examination, and his younger brother was Shu 澍. His wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

具慶下 弟弘曾 弘憲 弘賓 弘寅 弘賓 弘宸 弘宬 弘寰 娶馮氏

punctuated:
蔡茂春〔貫順天府三河縣民籍，福建福州府閩縣人，國子生，治詩經，字元卿，行一，年三十四，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖振，祖進，父義〔所吏目〕，母林氏。具慶下，弟華春、芳春、蕃春，娶章氏。順天府鄉試第二十名，會試第一名。

吳椿〔貫江西南昌府新建縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字壽卿，行二，年三十五，二月十三日生〕。曾祖玉，祖鳳，父必遂，母李氏。永感下，兄相，娶熊氏。江西鄉試第八名，會試第五十八名。

張烈〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，府學附學生，治書經，字明建，行一，年三十九，九月二十八日生〕。曾祖汴〔七品散官〕，祖松〔知州〕，父元昌，母李氏。重慶下，兄克承〔監生〕，弟紹祖、纘祖、緝祖、士光、勲、煦，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第二名，會試第四名。

黃宏宇〔貫太醫院醫籍，廣東瓊州府瓊山縣人，國子生，治詩經，字震祥，行一，年三十六，一月二十八日生〕。曾祖遂，祖通〔贈刑部主事〕，父顯〔按察司副使〕，母林氏。具慶下，弟弘宙、弘憲〔貢士〕、弘寅、弘實、弘宸、弘宬、弘寰，娶馮氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十五名，會試第四十名。
translation_en:
Cai Maochun, registered in a civilian household in Sanhe County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a native of Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanqing; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Jin; his father, Yi, an office clerk; and his mother, née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Huachun, Fangchun, and Fanchun. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chun, registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shouqing; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Feng; his father, Bisui; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xiang. He married a woman née Xiong. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lie, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingjian; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Bian, who held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Song, a prefect; his father, Yuanchang; and his mother, née Li. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His elder brother was Kecheng, a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Shaozu, Zuanzu, Jizu, Shiguang, Xun, and Xu. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Hongyu, registered in a medical household under the Imperial Medical Office, was a native of Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhenxiang; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Sui; his grandfather, Tong, posthumously appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Xian, a surveillance vice commissioner; and his mother, née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hongzhou, Hongxian, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Hongyin, Hongshi, Hongchen, Hongcheng, and Honghuan. He married a woman née Feng. He placed 125th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
朱奎〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字季文，行四，年三十八，正月十一日生〕。曾祖邦彥，祖質，父華，前母曽氏，母吳氏。永感下，兄燁、炳、煒，弟熯、本中，娶黃氏，繼娶涂氏、李氏。江西鄉試第八十二名，會試第五十二名。

毛為光〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字龍伯，行二十三，年三十一，十一月二十七日生〕。曾祖習，祖紳〔典膳〕，父榦，母屠氏，繼母王氏。重慶下，弟步光、灱光，娶陸氏。浙江鄉試第二十六名，會試第二百六十七名。

林澄源〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字仲源，行二，年二十四，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖黼，祖少陵，父師道，母徐氏。具慶下，兄瀾、逢源，弟漳、達源、洙、泳源、潮、濰，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十五名，會試第六十五名。

陳懋興〔貫福建福州府侯官縣民籍，福清縣人，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字德甫，行三，年二十三，八月十七日生〕。曾祖文珏，祖敷，父遷，母林氏。具慶下，兄賓興、復興，弟士興，娶謝氏。福建鄉試第十五名，會試第四十四名。
translation_en:
Zhu Kui, registered in an artisan household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jiwen; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bangyan, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Hua; his father's former wife was née Zeng, and his mother was née Wu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ye, Bing, and Wei, and his younger brothers Han and Benzhong. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently women née Tu and Li. He placed eighty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Weiguang, registered in a commoner household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Longbo; he ranked twenty-third in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xi, his grandfather Shen, a Steward of Provisions, and his father Gan; his mother was née Tu, and his stepmother née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Buguang and Xiaoguang. He married a woman née Lu. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Chengyuan, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongyuan; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Shaoling, and his father Shidao; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lan and Fengyuan, and his younger brothers Zhang, Dayuan, Zhu, Yongyuan, Chao, and Wei. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Maoxing, registered in a commoner household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and a native of Fuqing County, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-three years old, born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenjue, his grandfather Fu, and his father Qian; his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Binxing and Fuxing, and his younger brother Shixing. He married a woman née Xie. He placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃翼〔貫湖廣長沙衛官籍，直隸無為州人，國子生，治易經，字子南，行四，年三十二，四月十七日生〕。曾祖忠〔正千戶〕，祖虎〔正千戶〕，父恩〔指揮僉事〕，母謝氏。具慶下，兄宗〔指揮僉事〕、斗、胃，弟軫、壁，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第三十一名，會試第四十七名。

張祥鳶〔貫直隸鎮江府金壇縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字道卿，行七，年三十五，十一月十九日生〕。曾祖昶，祖鵬，父楫，母孫氏。具慶下，兄祥鯉、祥熊、祥鮫，弟祥鳧〔監生〕、祥煇、祥鸞、祥麃，娶虞氏。應天府鄉試第七十名，會試第二百二名。

吳紹〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉興縣民籍，秀水縣人，國子生，治書經，字汝復，行三，年二十四，十一月二十九日生〕。曾祖昭〔贈資政大夫吏部尚書〕，祖方〔贈資政大夫吏部尚書〕，父鵬〔吏部尚書〕，母戴氏〔封夫人〕。具慶下，兄繼〔後軍都督府都事〕、繪〔中書舍人〕，弟紳〔監生〕、經、綸、纘、緒、綬，娶郁氏，繼娶顧氏。順天府鄉試第三名，會試第二百二十五名。

張仲謙〔貫直隸松江府上海縣民籍，華亭縣人，國子生，治詩經，字士益，行二，年三十二，正月十九日生〕。曾祖昪〔州判官〕，祖峚〔府通判〕，父朝封，母王氏。重慶下，兄震伯，弟觀叔、仲頤、仲升、季履，娶顧氏。應天府鄉試第一百十名，會試第二十四名。
translation_en:
Huang Yi, registered in an official household of Changsha Guard, Huguang, was a native of Wuwei Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zinan and was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Zhong and grandfather Hu were battalion commanders; his father En was an assistant commander, and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zong, an assistant commander, Dou, and Wei; his younger brothers were Zhen and Bi. His wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xiangyuan was registered in a military household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Daoqing and was seventh in birth order, aged thirty-five, born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Peng, his father Ji, and his mother née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiangli, Xiangxiong, and Xiangjiao; his younger brothers were Xiangfu, an Imperial University student, Xianghui, Xiangluan, and Xiangpao. His wife was née Yu. He placed seventieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shao, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a native of Xiushui County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Rufu and was third in birth order, aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Zhao and grandfather Fang were each posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Assisting Governance and Minister of Personnel. His father Peng was Minister of Personnel; his mother, née Dai, was invested with the title Lady. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji, an office manager in the Chief Military Commission of the Rear Army, and Hui, a Secretariat drafter; his younger brothers were Shen, an Imperial University student, Jing, Lun, Zuan, Xu, and Shou. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Gu. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhongqian, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Huating County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shiyi and was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Bian was a subprefectural judge; his grandfather Mi was an assistant prefect. His father was Chaofeng, and his mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Zhenbo; his younger brothers were Guanshu, Zhongyi, Zhongsheng, and Jilü. His wife was née Gu. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Ji, courtesy name Bangchen, was registered in a civilian household in Sizhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wenchun; his grandfather, Yanhua; his father, Zhong; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun, and Gang; his younger brothers were Wei, Hui, Shen, Chun, Gao, Shou, Shao, and Hui [the transcription repeats 繪, Hui, here; ?]. He married a woman née Ji and subsequently a woman née Dong. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Qiyuan, courtesy name Daoqing, was registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Jiashan County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Du, a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Fu, was granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; and his father, Mi, was Right Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father's former wife, née Sheng, was posthumously granted the title of Ruren (Lady); his mother, also née Sheng, was granted the same title. His mother alone survived. His younger brother Qinan was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Qian. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Wan, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Tianhe; his grandfather, Yan; his father, Tianli; his mother, née Wang; and his stepmother, née Wu. His father alone survived. His younger brothers were Wang and Chong. He married a woman née Lin. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yinglin, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a guardsman's household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Qing; his father, Jian; and his mother, née Hao. His mother alone survived. His elder brother was Yingfeng. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bao Bian, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuanjing; he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and male cousins and was forty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jun, honorarily appointed Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Ding, a Prefect advanced to the prestige rank of Grand Master of the Second Rank; his father was Ping, and his mother was née Yuan. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hong, a tribute student; Hao; Yong, granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; Lian; Han; Jie 節, a Censor; Shen; Jie 潔; and Xiao, a Censor. His younger brothers were Fa, Ze, Pu, and Zhe. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Da Qidao, registered in an artisan household in Ren County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xingfu; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-nine years old, born on the ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Zhiyi, his father Chen, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother Yuan was a tribute student. His wife was née Luo. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jin, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked thirty-eighth among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-nine years old, born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Lei, honorarily appointed Prefectural Vice Prefect and additionally granted the posthumous title of Administration Vice Commissioner. His grandfather was Tingjing, a Subprefectural Assistant Magistrate who received successive posthumous honors culminating in the title of Left Administration Vice Commissioner. His father was Huan, Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his mother, née Hu, received successive honorary titles culminating in that of Lady of Virtue. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Bi; Chi, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Sheng, Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy. His younger brother was Shu. His wife was née Xie; he subsequently married a woman née Mao. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Xiangru, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daxing; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was thirty-five years old, born on the twelfth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather was Bi, granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; his father was 𩆩 [reading uncertain]; and his mother was née Yao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xiangqing, Xiangcai, and Xiangsheng. His wife was née Gu; he subsequently married a woman née Wu. He placed fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張光漢〔貫河南彰德府磁州武安縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字為章，行七，年三十八，六月十三日生〕。曾祖桓〔倉副使〕，祖璣〔縣丞〕，父儆，母李氏。具慶下。兄時舉、時用、時盛、時可、光宇、時學，弟時禮、光治、光泮、時得、時動、時與、時睦。娶温氏。河南鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百五十五名。

劉一儒〔貫湖廣荆州府夷陵州，民籍，州學生，治詩經，字學孔，行一，年二十三，正月十四日生〕。曾祖允清，祖漢，父大賓〔歲貢生〕，母秦氏。重慶下。弟一卿、一相。娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第八十三名，會試第五十四名。
translation_en:
Wang Yuanjing, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingchen. He ranked eleventh in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhang, his grandfather Wei, and his father Yi; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanchun, Left Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice, and Yuande; his younger brother was Yuanji. His wife was née Mao. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Xuebo, registered in Xiaogan County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Jinyue. He ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Mu (𥠇); his father’s former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xueyan, Prefectural Judge of Yingtian Prefecture, Xuezeng, Xuesi, and Xuemeng; his younger brothers were Xuewen, Xuebian, Xueshi, Xuexing, Xuegu, and Xueda. His wife was née Tang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Guanghan, registered in Wu’an County, Cizhou Subprefecture, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weizhang. He ranked seventh in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan, a Vice Commissioner of a Granary; his grandfather was Ji, a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Jing, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shiju, Shiyong, Shisheng, Shike, Guangyu, and Shixue; his younger brothers were Shili, Guangzhi, Guangpan, Shide, Shidong, Shiyu, and Shimu. His wife was née Wen. He placed thirty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yiru, registered in Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xuekong. He ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-three, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunqing, his grandfather Han, and his father Dabin, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Qin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yiqing and Yixiang. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eighty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陶幼學〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字子行，行十，年三十五，六月初十日生〕。曾祖愫，祖試〔訓導〕，父廷奎〔武學訓導，封監察御史〕，母商氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下。兄大有〔知府〕、惟學、大年〔布政司參議〕、承學〔知府〕，弟大順〔貢士〕、大信〔翰林院編修〕、勉學、来學、時學、典學、永學、禾學、享學。娶姜氏。浙江鄉試第二十三名，會試第一百五十三名。

吕鳴珂〔貫錦衣衛官籍，浙江處州府麗水縣人，順天府學生，治書經，字聲甫，行二，年三十，二月初一日生〕。曾祖璧〔贈懷遠將軍〕，祖文英〔封懷遠將軍、錦衣衛指揮同知〕，父昇〔州同知〕，前母陳氏〔贈孺人〕，母王氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下。兄鳴岐、鳴瑒，弟鳴珮〔文思院副使〕。娶王氏。順天府鄉試第四十四名，會試第二百九十四名。

translation_en:
Tao Youxue, registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zixing; he ranked tenth in the family and was thirty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Su; his grandfather, Shi, was an Assistant Instructor; and his father, Tingkui, was an Assistant Instructor in a military school, honorarily appointed Investigating Censor. His mother, née Shang, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dayou, a Prefect; Weixue; Danian, an Assistant Administration Commissioner; and Chengxue, a Prefect. His younger brothers were Dashun, a tribute scholar; Daxin, a Hanlin Academy Compiler; Mianxue; Laixue; Shixue; Dianxue; Yongxue; Hexue; and Xiangxue. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Mingke was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and came from Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Shengfu, ranked second in the family, and was thirty years old, born on the first day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Bi, was posthumously granted the title General Who Cherishes the Distant (Huaiyuan jiangjun). His grandfather, Wenying, was honorarily granted that title and the office of Vice Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His father, Sheng, was a Subprefect. His father's former wife, née Chen, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his mother, née Wang, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mingqi and Mingchang; his younger brother, Mingpei, was Vice Director of the Institute of Imperial Handicrafts. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Jun, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixi; he ranked sixth in the family and was thirty-four years old, born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Li, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Mengfu; his father, Pi, was a Prefectural Registrar; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chou; Ji, an Investigating Censor; Zhang, an Assistant Administration Commissioner; Tian; and Sixing, a tribute scholar. His younger brothers were Dong; Yuan, a tribute scholar; Lian; and Kan, a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Daodong, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingwu; he ranked first in the family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanying; his grandfather was Xiu; his father was Lian; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Daonan. He married a woman née Hu. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

蔡國熙〔貫直隸廣平府永年縣匠籍，府學生，治書經，字夢羲，行二，生年二十八，三月十九日生〕。曾祖智，祖芳，父廷光，母李氏。重慶下，弟國相、國賓，娶郭氏。順天府鄉試第三十四名，會試第三十六名。

曹一鳳〔貫山東青州府安丘縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字伯儀，行三，年二十六，十一月二十七日生〕。曾祖騰〔歲貢生〕，祖光漢〔歲貢生〕，父汝勤〔歲貢生〕，母王氏。重慶下，兄一麒、一麟〔進士〕，弟一鶴、一鯨、一豸、一鶚，娶周氏。山東鄉試第六十六名，會試第一百名。

陳成甫〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字光韶，行八，年三十九，二月初六日生〕。曾祖祀宗，祖仕律，父璉，嫡母周氏，生母莊氏。嚴侍下，弟成岳，娶馮氏。浙江鄉試第七十五名，會試第三十名。

林奇廸〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，府學增廣生，治書經，字敏教，行二，年三十二，六月十八日生〕。曾祖樟〔府通判〕，祖煥，父紹休，前母鄭氏、朱氏，母郭氏。慈侍下，兄化，娶張氏。福建鄉試第八名，會試第五十一名。
translation_en:
Cai Guoxi, registered in an artisan household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, directly administered territory, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mengxi; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight sui, born on the nineteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Fang, his father Tingguang, and his mother née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Guoxiang and Guobin, and his wife was née Guo. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Yifeng, registered in a civilian household in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Boyi; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-six sui, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Teng, grandfather Guanghan, and father Ruqin were all annual tribute students; his mother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Yiqi and Yilin, the latter a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his younger brothers were Yihe, Yijing, Yizhi, and Yi’e. His wife was née Zhou. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chengfu, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Guangshao; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was thirty-nine sui, born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sizong, his grandfather Shilü, and his father Lian; his legal mother was née Zhou and his birth mother née Zhuang. His father was his surviving parent. His younger brother was Chengyue, and his wife was née Feng. He placed seventy-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Qidi, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Minjiao; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang, an assistant prefect; his grandfather was Huan and his father Shaoxiu. His father’s former wives were née Zheng and née Zhu, and his mother was née Guo. His mother was his surviving parent. His elder brother was Hua, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄

translation_en:
Zhang Qiao, courtesy name Hengru, was registered in an officer household of the Yunnan Right Guard and was a native of Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Fen; and his father, Ji, Right Administrator. His mother was née Qian. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Zi, Dong, and Pu, and his wife was née Guo. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and one hundred eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Xiao, courtesy name Kezhong, was registered in an artisan household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongxin, Assistant Prefect; his grandfather, Tingzan; and his father, Shixian. His mother was née Zheng, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xuehou. His wife was née Jia; he subsequently married a woman née Jiang. He placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Zhenji, courtesy name Kong’an, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taixue; his grandfather, Zhengmin; and his father, Yongchang. His mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Diji and Qianji, and his younger brothers were Yuanji and Xiuji. His wife was née Peng. He placed ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kuizhou, courtesy name Ruyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Yangcheng County, Zezhou Subprefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, Vice Magistrate; his grandfather, Kun; and his father, Yue. His mother was née Wu. His father alone was living. His younger brother was Yongzhou, and his wife was née Guo. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yin Ru 尹儒, courtesy name Zizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Suizhou, De'an Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Long, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Chang; his mother was née Yao. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Tan. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gui Zhiyang 桂枝揚, courtesy name Mengyuan, was registered in a civilian household in De'an County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Xuan was a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Tingbi, and his father Shu was an Imperial University student. His father's principal wife was née Sun, and his birth mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhizhen, Zhigong, Zhihui, and Zhiting; his wife was née Zeng. He ranked twenty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ji 楊吉, courtesy name Menglong, was registered in a civilian household in Fushi County, Yan'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun. His grandfather Wei was a Professor in the establishment of the Prince of Shu and was posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father Benshen was an Investigating Censor. His father's former wife, née Zhen, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren); his mother, née Hu, was granted the same title. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhi and Wei; his younger brothers were Zhao, a Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and Li. His wife was née Liu. He ranked fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Zhen 錢鎮, courtesy name Shouzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Bin, and his father Yu; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Qin, and his younger brother Xi was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Mao. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zeng Tongheng, registered in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuye; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zeng Keshao; his grandfather, Zeng Bochong, had been granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites; his father, Zeng Cunren, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Luo, had been granted the title of Lady (ruren). His mother alone survived. His elder brother was Lin, and his younger brothers were Gong, Qianheng (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and Fuheng. His wife was née Liu. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Zhao, registered in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chaoxuan; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sun Ming; his grandfather, Sun Jiang; his father, Sun Neng; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yingke. His wife was née Zhong, and his subsequent wife was née Yu. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Qicai, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jiqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin Chen; his grandfather, Lin Jing; his father, Lin Han; and his mother, née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qiwu, Qipian, Qizi, and Qishao. His wife was née Zhuang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ruhai, registered in Yi County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruhui; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang Xuan, Director in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather, Wang Yi; his father, Wang Daheng; and his mother, née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Rushui and Chaojing (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and his younger brothers were Chaoyuan, Ruchuan, Rulan, and Rushan. His wife was née Zhang. He placed seventy-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
范燧〔貫陝西西安府同州郃陽縣軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字以木，行一，年三十五，八月十九日生〕。曾祖錦，祖廷臣，父棟，母韓氏。重慶下，弟灼，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第二十五名，會試第五十六名。

沈奎〔貫直隸常州府江陰縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字文叔，行二，年三十五，九月二十六日生〕。曾祖信，祖厚，父元，母袁氏。慈侍下，兄問〔省祭官〕，娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第九十三名，會試第二百四十名。

劉大遣〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，儒士，治易經，字廷植，行一，年二十七，七月二十九日生〕。曾祖鴻，祖騰〔典史〕，父萬，母童氏。永感下，兄廷賓，娶林氏。福建鄉試第四十一名，會試第九名。

李學禮〔貫直隸鳳陽府潁州民籍，府學生，治易經，字子立，行二，年三十一，十二月初八日生〕。曾祖宣，祖玉，父臣，母張氏。慈侍下，兄學詩，弟學易，娶蔡氏。應天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第一百二十三名。
translation_en:
Fan Sui, registered in a military household in Heyang County, Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yimu; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-five, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Tingchen, his father Dong, and his mother née Han. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Zhuo, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Kui, registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenshu; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-five, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Hou, his father Yuan, and his mother née Yuan. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother Wen was a Sacrificial Official [?], and his wife was née Wu. He placed ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Daqian, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingzhi; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Teng was a Chief Clerk, his father was Wan, and his mother was née Tong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingbin, and his wife was née Lin. He placed forty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xueli, registered in a civilian household in Yingzhou, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural-school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zili; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-one, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Yu, his father Chen, and his mother née Zhang. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His elder brother was Xueshi, his younger brother Xueyi, and his wife was née Cai. He placed ninety-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

周聚星〔貫浙江金華府永康縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字文卿，行一百九，年三十二，三月初十日生〕。曾祖仲悌，祖瑩，父鍾，母王氏。重慶下，弟聚奎、聚昴、聚翼，娶王氏。浙江鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百六名。

王葑〔貫浙江處州府麗水縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字德孚，行二，年三十一，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖福，祖瓔，父琴，母羅氏。具慶下，兄蕋，娶林氏。浙江鄉試第八十五名，會試第一百二十八名。

趙宋〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州興化縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子隆，行一，年二十八，六月二十四日生〕。曾祖綸，祖潤，父雱，母費氏，繼母徐氏。具慶下，弟寀、榘、臬、模、禾，娶陸氏。應天府鄉試第六十七名，會試第九十三名。

胡僖〔貫浙江金華府蘭谿縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字伯安，行十七，年三十八，八月初二日生〕。曾祖宗愷，祖益，父富，母鄭氏。具慶下，兄仁、傑、傳，弟佩，娶宋氏。浙江鄉試第三十一名，會試第一百三十名。
translation_en:
Zhou Juxing, registered in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Wenqing, ranked 109th in his family’s birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongti, his grandfather Ying, his father Zhong, and his mother née Wang; his parents and grandparents were living; his younger brothers were Jukui, Jumao, and Juyi; his wife was née Wang; he placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Feng, registered in Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Defu, ranked second in his family’s birth order, and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Ying, his father Qin, and his mother née Luo; both parents were living; his elder brother was Rui; his wife was née Lin; he placed eighty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Song, registered in Xinghua County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county Confucian school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Zilong, ranked first in his family’s birth order, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Run, his father Pang, his mother née Fei, and his stepmother née Xu; his father and stepmother were living; his younger brothers were Cai, Ju, Nie, Mo, and He; his wife was née Lu; he placed sixty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xi, registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Bo’an, ranked seventeenth in his family’s birth order, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongkai, his grandfather Yi, his father Fu, and his mother née Zheng; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Ren, Jie, and Chuan, and his younger brother was Pei; his wife was née Song; he placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
吳兌〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字君澤，行七，年三十五，四月二十日生〕。曾祖源〔封南京刑部主事〕，祖便〔按察司副使〕，父意，母周氏。慈侍下，兄恒、恂、忱〔監生〕，弟恮、充、沈、忡、志、念，娶駱氏。順天府鄉試第四十五名，會試第三十五名。

應存卓〔貫浙江台州府僊居縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字從之，行五，年二十九，閏六月十九日生〕。曾祖巨，祖匡〔贈吏部主事，加贈工部員外郎〕，父大猷〔刑部郎中〕，前母秦氏〔贈安人〕，母彭氏〔封安人〕，生母高氏。具慶下，兄存初〔監生〕、存默、存性〔工部主事〕、存修、存畏，弟存素、存徵、存章，娶侯氏。浙江鄉試第九十名，會試第一百十八名。

李穟〔貫順天府薊州，民籍，州學生，治書經，字伯實，行三，年三十二，正月十三日生〕。曾祖文友，祖敖，父果〔贈監察御史〕，嫡母郭氏〔贈孺人〕，生母庾氏。慈侍下，兄秋〔監察御史〕、秩，弟稙、穩，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第九十三名，會試第九十六名。

錢藻〔貫直隸揚州府泰州如皐縣，匠籍，縣學生，治易經，字自文，行二，年二十六，十月十八日生〕。曾祖玘，祖轍〔縣丞〕，父岳，母吳氏。嚴侍下，兄激，弟潔、淵、演、濱、浚，娶許氏。應天府鄉試第一百十六名，會試第一百五十九名。
translation_en:
Wu Dui 吳兌, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Junze, he ranked seventh in family order, and he was thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Bian, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his father was Yi, and his mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Heng, Xun, and Chen, the last a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Quan, Chong, Shen, Chong, Zhi, and Nian. His wife was née Luo. He placed forty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ying Cunzhuo 應存卓, registered in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Congzhi, he ranked fifth in family order, and he was twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the intercalary sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ju; his grandfather was Kuang, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and subsequently that of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; and his father was Dayou, Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father's former wife, née Qin, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren); his mother, née Peng, was granted the same title; and his birth mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cunchu, a student of the Directorate of Education, Cunmo, Cunxing, Secretary in the Ministry of Works, Cunxiu, and Cunwei; his younger brothers were Cunsu, Cunzheng, and Cunzhang. His wife was née Hou. He placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Sui 李穟, registered in Ji Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Boshi, he ranked third in family order, and he was thirty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wenyou; his grandfather was Ao; and his father was Guo, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His principal mother, née Guo, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren); his birth mother was née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qiu, Investigating Censor, and Zhi; his younger brothers were Zhi and Wen. His wife was née Zhang. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Zao 錢藻, registered in Rugao County, Tai Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to an artisan household and was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziwen, he ranked second in family order, and he was twenty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather was Zhe, County Vice Magistrate; his father was Yue; and his mother was née Wu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Ji; his younger brothers were Jie, Yuan, Yan, Bin, and Jun. His wife was née Xu. He placed 116th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hua Ruli, courtesy name Yongcheng, was registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Dao, his father Zhi'an, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ruqi, and his wife was née Yang. He ranked eightieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Qinglong, courtesy name Yuxiang, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De, his grandfather Jiang, and his father Kun, an annual tribute student; his father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qinglin, an Instructor of Medicine, and Qingxiong. His wife was née Tan; he subsequently married a woman née Zhou. He ranked forty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Weipi, courtesy name Yugong, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congjiang, his grandfather Ruxin, his father Qiye, and his mother née Gu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Weiyi, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, and Weili; his wife was née Qin. He ranked forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Bangxian, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a military household in Gaochun County, Yingtian Prefecture. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged nineteen, and born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi; his grandfather Lie was posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; his father Shuyang was a Prefect; and his mother, née Huang, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother Bangli was a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Bangben and Bangda. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Guohua, registered in a military household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangshi; he ranked tenth in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Jin, and his father Huai. His father's former wives were Lady Fang and Lady Wang; his mother was Lady Lu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guotai, Guofan, Chao (an official awaiting selection for appointment), and Guoxiu; his younger brothers were Guowang, Guoqi, Guozuo, and Guobao. He married Lady Wang. He placed seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Mingshi, registered in an artisan household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shenfu; he ranked third in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Yu (a prestige official), and his father Yue (Vice Battalion Commander). His father's former wife was Lady Wang; his mother was Lady Qin. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mingchen and Mingru (Department Magistrate); his younger brothers were Mingfu and Mingbi. He married Lady Yu and subsequently Lady Zhang. He placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Shunshi, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Daolong; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tai (granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under an applicable regulation), his grandfather Yuanzhen, his father Tiren, and his mother Lady Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhixuan (Secretary in the Ministry of Justice); his younger brothers were Shunde, Shunli, Shunzhi, and Shunhua. He married Lady Bian. He placed 102nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ziren, registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Anfu; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Tinggui, his grandfather Shouping (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions), his father Jiong, and his mother Lady Yuan. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Ziyi, Zidao, Zida, Zizhong, and Zili. He married Lady Lu. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

戈九疇〔貫錦衣衛匠籍，直隸蘇州府吳縣人，國子生，治禮記，字惟範，行一，年三十四，六月十二日生〕。曾祖昇〔壽官〕，祖麟〔訓導〕，父貴〔七品散官〕，前母湯氏，母王氏。慈侍下，兄九功、九韶、九成、九德、九章〔苑馬寺少卿〕、九儀，弟九經，娶任氏。順天府鄉試第九十三名，會試第二百七十三名。

游醇卿〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字原學，行一，年三十七，九月二十六日生〕。曾祖克敏，祖紹慶，父奎，母汪氏。永感下，弟立卿、文卿、時卿，娶汪氏，繼娶汪氏。應天府鄉試第一百十二名，會試第二百九名。
translation_en:
Wang Wen, courtesy name Weizhen, was registered in a civilian household in Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A county-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was En, a county magistrate posthumously granted the title of Left Vice Censor-in-Chief; his father was Dechun, a county vice magistrate; and his mother was née Sun. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yin, a prefectural vice prefect, Wen, and Fa, a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Que, Kai, a tribute scholar, Guan, and Min. His wife was née Pei. He placed one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Zhiping, courtesy name Weibang, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked fourth in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather was Dayong; his father was He, a county magistrate; his mother was née Guo; and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guo, Gui, Zhidong, and Zhilong; his younger brothers were Zhiqiao, Zhihong, Zhikun, Zhihan, Zhifan, and Zhiyuan. His wife was née Xiao. He placed forty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Jiuchou, courtesy name Weifan, was registered in an artisan household under the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Lin, an assistant instructor; and his father was Gui, a seventh-rank titular official. His father's former wife was née Tang, and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Jiugong, Jiushao, Jiucheng, Jiude, Jiuzhang, vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and Jiuyi; his younger brother was Jiujing. His wife was née Ren. He placed ninety-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Chunqing, courtesy name Yuanxue, was registered in a military household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kemin; his grandfather was Shaoqing; his father was Kui; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Liqing, Wenqing, and Shiqing. His first wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was also née Wang. He placed one hundred twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡廷黼〔貫湖廣長沙府瀏陽縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字元素，行十七，年三十七，五月十一日生〕。曾祖志寛，祖凱正，父大韶〔歲貢生〕，母彭氏，繼母王氏。慈侍下，弟廷黻、廷黼，娶黎氏。湖廣鄉試第六十六名，會試第二十八名。

宋豫卿〔貫四川敘州府富順縣民籍，江西臨江府新淦縣人，府學生，治詩經，字子樂，行二，年二十九，八月二十六日生〕。曾祖萬智，祖安遠，父用，母陳氏。具慶下，兄履卿，弟泰卿、臨卿、益卿、晉卿、復卿，娶劉氏。四川鄉試第六名，會試第一百二十名。

張尚大〔貫江西吉安府萬安縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字時豐，行三，年三十五，十一月初三日生〕。曾祖履安，祖顯〔旌表孝子〕，父鋭，母蕭氏。具慶下，兄尚禮、尚文，弟尚象，娶陳氏。江西鄉試第三十四名，會試第二百五十九名。
translation_en:
Jia Xuan, registered in an artisan household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shunju; he ranked second in his family and was aged forty, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather was Ning; his father was Xiyan, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Feng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Qian, and his younger brothers were Jiong, Shu, Da, Sui, Yu, Xun, Cong, Pin, and Sheng. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Tingfu, registered in a military household in Liuyang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuansu; he ranked seventeenth in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhikuan; his grandfather was Kaizheng; his father was Dashao, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Peng, and his stepmother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Tingfu 廷黻 and Tingfu 廷黼 [the latter repeats the candidate’s own name: ?]. His wife was née Li. He placed sixty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yuqing, registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, and originally from Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zile; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wanzhi; his grandfather was Anyuan; his father was Yong; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lüqing, and his younger brothers were Taiqing, Linqing, Yiqing, Jinqing, and Fuqing. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shangda, registered in a civilian household in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shifeng; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Lü’an; his grandfather was Xian, officially commended for filial piety; his father was Rui; and his mother was née Xiao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shangli and Shangwen, and his younger brother was Shangxiang. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈節甫〔貫浙江湖州府烏程縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字以安，行一，年二十七，三月十一日生〕。曾祖汝梁，祖端〔貢士〕，父塾，母閔氏。重慶下，弟之鎏、之鍪、之鑅、之堣、之鋻、之鍳、之鋈、之鐆、之鉒、之鎰，娶唐氏。浙江鄉試第五十九名，會試第二十五名。

translation_en:
Ye Xian 葉憲, courtesy name Decheng, was registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked tenth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Siqi, his grandfather Jingtong, his father Jun, and his mother née Yuan. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Yuan and Shu; his younger brothers were Mao, Hui, Que, and Yi. He married a woman née Xiong. He placed seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Gu 歐陽穀, courtesy name Zhongsi, was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked third among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Guangben, his grandfather Dunfu, and his father Xiang. His legal mother was née Xie and his birth mother née Xiong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhi, He, Qiu, Ji, and Qin; his younger brothers were Xin and Ying. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Jiefu 沈節甫, courtesy name Yi’an, was registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ruliang, his grandfather Duan (a tribute student), his father Shu, and his mother née Min. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zhiliu, Zhimou, Zhiheng, Zhiyu, Zhijian 之鋻, Zhijian 之鍳, Zhiwu, Zhisui, Zhizhu, and Zhiyi. He married a woman née Tang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fenyong 劉奮庸, courtesy name Shike, was registered in a military household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Guan, his father Jimin (a district magistrate), and his mother née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Dengyong (a tribute student), and his younger brother Zhengyong. He married a woman née Du. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

林燦章〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，府學生，治書經，字繼顯，行一，年三十三，四月初六日生〕。曾祖與飾，祖師順〔封禮部主事，贈按察司副使〕，父應標〔左布政使〕，母陳氏〔封恭人〕。慈侍下，弟炫章、煥章、耀章、烶章〔刑部郎中〕、烺章。娶黃氏，繼娶卓氏。福建鄉試第七十四名，會試第一百二十六名。

田汝頴〔貫山東濟南府武定州信陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字登之，行五，年三十一，六月二十二日生〕。曾祖泳，祖山，父渠，前母劉氏，母邊氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄汝秀、汝芳、汝栗、汝堅，弟汝碩、汝頔。娶孟氏。山東鄉試第一名，會試第三十二名。
translation_en:
Lin Canzhang 林燦章 was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Jixian and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yushi; his grandfather, Shishun, received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Rites and the posthumous title of Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father, Yingbiao, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and his mother, née Chen, received the title Lady of Respect. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Xuanzhang, Huanzhang, Yaozhang, Tingzhang (a Director in the Ministry of Justice), and Langzhang. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Zhuo. He placed seventy-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Ruying 田汝頴 was registered in Xinyang County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Dengzhi and ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Shan; and his father, Qu. His father's former wife was née Liu, his mother was née Bian, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruxiu, Rufang, Ruli, and Rujian; his younger brothers were Rushuo and Rudi. He married a woman née Meng. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳紹登〔貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍，江陰縣人，府學附學生，治詩經，字誕先，行一，年二十七，三月十三日生〕。曾祖叔端，祖政，父崇慶〔按察司僉事〕，前母王氏，母唐氏。重慶下，弟仲登、繼登，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第九十一名，會試第一百四十四名。

translation_en:
Third Class: 225 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Wang Shu, courtesy name Yifu, was registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a native of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunshou (Consort, granted the honorary rank of Grand Master for Central Service); his grandfather was Chaoqing (a metropolitan graduate); and his father was Jian (Assistant Prefect). His mother was née Kang, and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shi (a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year) and Shu. He married a woman née Ai. He placed seventy-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shaodeng, courtesy name Danxian, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Jiangyin County. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuduan; his grandfather was Zheng; and his father was Chongqing (Surveillance Commissioner’s Assistant). His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother née Tang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongdeng and Jideng. He married a woman née Wang. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Zhi, courtesy name Zirong, was registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Qiantang County. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Zongfu; and his father was Hui. His mother was née Yao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Song, Bai, Huai, and Chun (an official awaiting selection for appointment); his younger brothers were Gui, Shu, Pian, Pu, Nan, and Mei. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Lin. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cui Dong, registered in a civilian household in Biyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Longji; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Zhou, and his father Ran; his mother was née Shang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Nan, Pu, Ge, Quan, and Shi, and his wife was née Jiao. He ranked forty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Yigui, registered in a military household of Zhongyi Central Guard in Shuntian Prefecture and a native of Gucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zigao; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, his grandfather Jie, and his father Mei; his father's principal wife was née Xi, and his birth mother was née Li. His mother survived his father. His younger brothers were Yilong and Yilin, and his wife was née Jia. He ranked thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Jiaji, registered in a salt-producing household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaoshuo; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ji and grandfather Yu each held the honorary title of Official for Righteous Service; his father was Chi, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiade and Jiaye, and his wife was née Qu. He ranked twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Weixin, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Wenhua; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the sixteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather Xuan was Salt Transport Commissioner and was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of the Palace. His father An was Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission, and his mother, née Xie, was granted the title Lady of Repose. His father survived his mother. His elder brothers were Shaozu and Jingxian; his younger brothers were Weide, Weixin 維信, Weixian, Weilie, Weiming, Weizhen, and Weiyue. His wife was née Chen. He ranked fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.
