黃襄〔貫福建泉州府南安縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字國著，行五，年三十四，十二月二十五日生〕。曾祖欽，祖澤，父柯，母楊氏。永感下，弟褧、裒、褒，娶李氏。福建鄉試第七十五名，會試第二百五十三名。
translation_en:
Xie Song 解宋 was registered in Xinghua County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in an artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingru. He was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Sizheng, his grandfather Qi, and his father Wen; his father's former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Yao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Su, Zhen, and Shi, and his wife was née Ding. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qigu 王期古 was registered in the Left Battalion of Luzhou Guard, Shanxi, in a military household. An added student of the Lu'an Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Kechun. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Gang and grandfather Yong both held honorary offices for longevity; his father Long was a Consort, and his mother was the Lady of Xiajin County. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qizhi, Qihua, and Qidao, and his wife was née Gan. He placed thirty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Ruhuan 燕儒宦 was registered in Lushan County, Ruzhou Subprefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yongdao. He was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Fengxian, his grandfather Guang, his father Ju, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruchen, his younger brother Rubin, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed fourteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xiang 黃襄 was registered in Nan'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Guozhu. He was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Ze, his father Ke, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jiong, Pou, and Bao, and his wife was née Li. He placed seventy-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Xing 陳省, courtesy name Kongzhen, was registered in a military household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Gan, was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; and his father, Dahuo, was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi). His mother was née Zhao, and his stepmother née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi, Qirui, Rui (Patrol Inspector), Rui (Investigating Censor), Mo, Shi (provincial graduate, juren), Xuan, Qi (tribute student), and Feng [the opening names in this list appear garbled; their division is uncertain]. His younger brothers were Biao, Shi, Wang, Hou, Qian, Gun, Zhuan, and Jian. His wife was née Zhuang. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Ruoyu 牛若愚, courtesy name Ruiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi, and was a native of Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Zheng, and grandfather, Zan, both held honorary offices conferred for longevity; his father, Yang, was a County School Instructor, and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Ruoqi and Ruoxu (tribute student); his younger brothers were Rulu, Ruone, and Ruohui. His wife was née Wu. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Hua 舒化, courtesy name Rude, was registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xiecheng; his grandfather was Yukuo; his father, Bi, was a County School Instructor; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Feng, Zuo, Jun, Jie, and Wei; his younger brother was Zhan. His wife was née Huang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yuerui 劉曰睿, courtesy name Rusi, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Bogong, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Works. His grandfather, Tingzhong, was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master for Fostering Good Government. His father, Shigui, was an Office Clerk in a suo office [the type of office is unspecified]. His father's former wife was née Wei, and his mother was née Gong. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yueyu (student of the Directorate of Education) and Yuexu; his younger brothers were Yuecai (Secretary in the Ministry of Rites), Yueqing, and Yuefu. His wife was née Jiang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lei Jigu, registered in a military household in En County, Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruzheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, an Instructor of Medicine; his grandfather was Yingjie; his father was Dian; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wangu, Shugu, Shigu, Chonggu, and Fugu. He married a woman née Fu. He placed twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhihan, registered in a civilian household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Xianqing; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Wan; his father was Ji; and his mother was née Hu. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang He, registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was an auxiliary county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Minggao; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather was Ming; his father was Tingzuo; and his mother was née Sun. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yuan, Hong, and Feng. He married a woman née Han. He placed fifty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Degong, registered in a civilian household in Guangshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zi'an; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was You, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Mu; his father was Zhuan; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Dewen. He married a woman née Cai and subsequently a woman née Zheng. He placed nineteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Maoxun, registered in a military household of Fuzhou Right Guard in Fujian and a native of Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruce; he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather An, and his father Chun; his father’s principal wife and his birth mother were both née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Maoyuan, Maoheng, Maozhen, and Maozhao; his younger brother was Maojian. He married a woman née Fang and subsequently a woman née Xia. He placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ruopan, registered in a military household of Guizhou Guard in Guizhou and a native of Jiangpu County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a student of the Pacification Commission’s school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenhua; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Xian, and his father Qing, a County Magistrate; his father’s principal wife was née Li and his birth mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ruosi. He married a woman née Cao. He placed third in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and one hundred seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Kejiao, registered in a civilian household of Cheng’an County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zishou; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was He, his grandfather Guo, and his father Shaoxian, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Liu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Kewei; his younger brothers were Kecheng, Kexian, a tribute scholar, Kejia, Kejing, and Kejiu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhen Pei, registered in an official household of Yutai County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruze; he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shi, his grandfather Heng, an honorary official, and his father Kai, a County Registrar; his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Pu, Pang, Pan, and Bian, the last an Imperial University student; his younger brother Jin was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort. He married a woman née Wang. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zha Zhilong, registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mingzhi. Seventh in birth order, he was twenty-six years old and was born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yi, honorifically appointed Grand Master for Governance and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his grandfather was Hui, posthumously appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites and additionally awarded the posthumous title Grand Master for Upright Service. His father was Bingzhi, a Director in the Ministry of Justice. His legal mother, née Ma, was posthumously titled Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Wu. His father was living, his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Zhixue (an Imperial University student), Zhixing, Zhiwen, Zhigao, Zhiqi (an Imperial University student), and Zhihong (a Metropolitan Examination graduate awaiting the Palace Examination); his younger brothers were Zhili (a Secretary in the Ministry of Rites), Zhiling (an Imperial University student), and Zhiwan. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chenglai, registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Liangfu. First in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Wenpu, his father Xiao, and his mother née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Chengxian, Chengming, Chengde, and Chengxiao. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Nan, registered in a civilian household in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Maocai. First in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Gong, his father Wenxuan, and his mother née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brother Gui was a Metropolitan Examination graduate awaiting the Palace Examination. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Du, registered in a civilian household in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanzhou. First in birth order, he was twenty-eight years old and was born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, an honorary official distinguished for longevity; his grandfather was Ao, a Director of Food Service, honorifically appointed Investigating Censor. His father was Yingzhen, an Imperial University student, and his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Weidong; his younger brothers were Shengdong, Geng, and Kuo. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Jingzhong, courtesy name Zixing, was registered in a military household in Tongling County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Yongjiang, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his father, Jie, was a Magistrate. His mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Luo; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hongzhong, Yizhong (a government-stipend student), Shizhong, and Qinzhong. His wife was née Ke. He placed eighteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Zimu, courtesy name Runan, was registered in a civilian household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Ao; and his father, Yingdeng, an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Zhu and his stepmother née Lu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zimei, Ziye, and Zimo; his younger brothers were Zihe, Zifu, Zibin, Zimao, Zijie, Zilai, Zimai, and Ziyin. His wife was née Yan. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Dongyang, courtesy name Zisheng, was registered in a military household of the Baoning Battalion in Sichuan and was originally from Baling County, Huguang. A Baoning prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather, Yi; and his father, Tingchen. His father's earlier wife was née Cui, his mother née Yang, and his stepmothers née Li and née Liu; both parents were living. His wife was née Yu, and his subsequent wife née Xu. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Yiyang, courtesy name Ziju, was registered in a military household in Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An added-quota student at the county government school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Zhong, held the honorary title of Official for Longevity; his grandfather, Jingren, was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; his father, Jikui, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Bao, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His father alone was living. His elder brothers, Yizai and Yiming, were students of the Imperial University; his younger brother was Yiyue. His wife was née Ren. He placed forty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jiabin, registered in a military household in Chong’an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ziyang, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jirong (an honorary official for longevity), his grandfather Wenya, his father Cong (a county school instructor), and his mother née Wu; his mother was living and his father deceased, he married a woman née Ji, and he ranked eighty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ru, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhenqing, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Shi, his father Xian, and his mother née Shen; both parents were living, his younger brother was Ren, he married a woman née Xu, and he ranked fifty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xianchen, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Qinbo, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Mian, his father Hong, and his mother née Guan; both parents were deceased, he married a woman née Pu, and he ranked 127th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Youxian, registered in a military household in Ningxiang County, Shizhou Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xiyao, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ling, his grandfather Ying, his father Yong (an honorary official for public beneficence), his legal mother née Zhang, and his birth mother née Tian; his mother was living and his father deceased, he married a woman née Liang and subsequently another woman née Liang, and he ranked fifty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

An additional student at the Shuntian Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruhe; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Jun, and his father Mao; his mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wenshi and Wenrong; his younger brothers were Wenguan, Wenzi, Wenxian, Wenzong, and Wenhuan. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Yang. He ranked fifty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yingjie 林應節 had civilian household registration in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shiqing; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Tijin, his grandfather Yuanzhen, and his father Ruxian, who had been granted the title of Guard Registrar. His father's former wife, née Fang, had been posthumously granted the title of Lady (ruren); his mother, née Zheng, had been granted the same title. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qing, a Subprefect; Ang, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and Yingbin, a Guard Registrar. His younger brother was Yingqi. He married a woman née Zheng. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Sizhu 李思柱 had civilian household registration in Wuyi County, Ji Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zisheng; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twentieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Qiang, his grandfather Zan, and his father Yi; his mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Sidong and his younger brother Sizhen. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Shoudao 俞守道 had civilian household registration in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daqing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Run, his grandfather Hua, and his father Can; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yuandao, Jidao, Jiandao, and Tidao. He married a woman née Jin. He ranked sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tianjue 王天爵 was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of She County, Huizhou Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Zixiu and ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qisun; his grandfather, He; his father, Tingzheng; his mother, née Min; and his stepmother, née Han. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tianyi, Tianfu, and Tian’ai. He married a woman surnamed Xu, and subsequently married another woman surnamed Xu and a woman surnamed Zhou. He placed 115th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Tingxuan 楊廷選 was registered in an artisan household under the Office of Discipline of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ziyong and ranked second among his brothers. He was twenty-seven, born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather, Ji; his father, Jin, an Instructor at the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Shen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Tingxiang, Tingxiu (Clepsydra Keeper in the Directorate of Astronomy), Tingzuo (Recorder in the Court of Imperial Entertainments), Tingru, and Tingjue; his younger brothers were Tingxian and Tingyou. He married a woman surnamed Yu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Xijing 趙熙靖 was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Jingke and ranked third among his brothers. He was thirty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather, Hui; his father, Shiru; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhongdao and Zhongfu; his younger brother was Zhonghe. He married a woman surnamed Bian. He placed ninety-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuren 王育仁 was registered in a military household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Yanhua and ranked second among his brothers. He was twenty-seven, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuejin; his grandfather, Guocheng; his father, Qinchen; and his mother, née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yude. He married a woman surnamed Zeng. He placed fifty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

賀邦泰〔貫直隸鎮江府丹陽縣軍籍，常州府武進縣人，縣學生，治詩經，字道卿，行一，年三十七，九月二十五日生〕。曾祖敦〔七品散官〕，祖璨〔封兵馬指揮〕，父鎬〔兵馬指揮〕，母巢氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，弟邦演、邦佐、邦靖、邦教、邦楨，娶鄧氏。應天府鄉試第七十二名，會試第一百七十七名。

周之屏〔貫湖廣長沙府湘潭縣馬船籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯卿，行一，年三十二，八月二十二日生〕。曾祖淦，祖思時〔壽官〕，父訓〔監生〕，母楊氏。重慶下，弟之翰〔貢士〕、之光、之基、之命、之龍，娶江氏，繼娶鄧氏。湖廣鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百二十四名。
translation_en:
Jing Wenzhao, courtesy name Shutao, was registered in a military household in Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Bian, his father Shu, and his mother née Feng; his father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wenbing, an Imperial University student, and Wenye, a tribute scholar; his younger brother was Wenhuan, an Imperial University student. His wife was née Xu. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Shi, courtesy name Daochong, was registered in a military household in Hongtong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the tenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Lun, his father Tinglu, and his mother née Wei; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Fu, and his wife was née Liu. He placed sixtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Bangtai, courtesy name Daoqing, was registered in a military household in Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dun, a seventh-rank prestige official; his grandfather was Can, granted the title of Commander of a Military Police Office; his father was Gao, Commander of a Military Police Office; and his mother was née Chao, granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bangyan, Bangzuo, Bangjing, Bangjiao, and Bangzhen, and his wife was née Deng. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zhiping, courtesy name Boqing, was registered in a horse-transport boat household in Xiangtan County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gan; his grandfather was Sishi, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Xun, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Yang. Parents and grandparental elders were living. His younger brothers were Zhihan, a tribute scholar, Zhiguang, Zhiji, Zhiming, and Zhilong. His wife was née Jiang, and he subsequently married a woman née Deng. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Jinsi, registered in Qinzhou, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a department-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Shan, and his father Zuo; his mother was née Lu and his stepmother née Wen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jinde, and his wife was née Yang. He placed eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Tang, registered in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a department-school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sijian, his grandfather Ding, and his father Ben𧅥 [second character uncertain, ?]; his mother was née He. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jia and Pin, his younger brother was Wen, and his wife was née Li. He placed twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Rizhang, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an附生 supplementary student of the county school, specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Xuejiong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangxian, his grandfather Xianke, and his father Desheng; his mother was née Hong. His mother alone was living. His younger brother Rijiu was a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his wife was née Chen. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shichun, registered in Anji Department, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Chengshu; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongmin, his grandfather Hong, and his father Mao; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shigang, an Assistant Instructor, and Shixiang; his younger brothers were Shilun, Shijin, Shiwei (士維), and Shiwei (士緯). His wife was née Wang. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

宋訓〔貫河南汝寧府新蔡縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝式，行一，年三十四，十二月初四日生〕。曾祖智，祖澤，父大經，母李氏。重慶下，兄揖，弟講、試、讃、許、調、訒、詞、桂，娶李氏。河南鄉試第七十三名，會試第一百八十三名。

随承業〔貫山東東昌府聊城縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字思顯，行三，年二十四，十一月十三日生〕。曾祖信，祖興，父祚，母張氏。具慶下，兄承訓、承恩，弟承寵，娶陳氏。山東鄉試第七名，會試第二百十名。
translation_en:
Ouyang Mo, courtesy name Hongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xia; his grandfather, Gao, held an honorary title for public benefaction; his father, Shen, was a commander appointed under precedent-based provisions; and his mother was née Hong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fuchu, and his younger brothers were Shu, Zhen, Nan, Zhu, Chun, and Cheng. His wife was née Huang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Guohua, courtesy name Liangshi, was registered in a civilian household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Hu, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, advanced in prestige rank to Grand Master for Excellent Counsel; his grandfather, Que, held an honorary title for longevity. His father was Benqing, his mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Ren. His parents were deceased. His elder brother, Guoyong, was an Investigating Censor; his younger brothers were Guojun and Guoyan. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed fifteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Xun, courtesy name Rushi, was registered in a civilian household in Xincai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Songs, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Ze; his father, Dajing; and his mother, née Li. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Yi, and his younger brothers were Jiang, Shi, Zan, Xu, Diao, Ren, Ci, and Gui. His wife was née Li. He placed seventy-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sui Chengye, courtesy name Sixian, was registered in a civilian household in Liaocheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Xing; his father, Zuo; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengxun and Cheng’en, and his younger brother was Chengchong. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李遷梧〔貫山東青州府安丘縣，軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字茂陽，行二，年三十一，四月初二日生〕。曾祖嵩，祖普，父完〔省祭官〕，母王氏，繼母丁氏。嚴侍下，兄遷喬〔貢士〕，弟遷槓、遷桐、遷梓，娶王氏。山東鄉試第四十名，會試第二百八十名。

沈如麒〔貫順天府霸州，民籍，浙江嘉興府嘉興縣人，國子生，治詩經，字朝珍，行二，年三十七，正月十五日生〕。曾祖盛，祖祥〔巡檢〕，父賢，母謝氏。永感下，兄如鳳，弟如麟，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第五十五名，會試第三十八名。

劉漢儒〔貫河南開封府陳州沈丘縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字文卿，行一，年二十八，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖德，祖釗，父東，母普氏。具慶下，弟漢傑，娶楊氏。河南鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百九十四名。
translation_en:
Gu Kui, registered in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Wenyao, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, a seventh-rank prestige official; his grandfather was Xu; his father was Shan; and his mother was née Sun. His mother alone survived. His younger brother was Zhen, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qianwu, registered in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Maoyang, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Song; his grandfather was Pu; his father was Wan, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan); his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Ding. His father alone survived. His elder brother was Qianqiao, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brothers were Qiangang, Qiantong, and Qianzi. His wife was née Wang. He placed fortieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Ruqi, registered in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Chaozhen, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Xiang, a Police Chief; his father was Xian; and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Rufeng, his younger brother was Rulin, and his wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Hanru, registered in Shenqiu County, Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Wenqing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Zhao; his father was Dong; and his mother was née Pu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Hanjie, and his wife was née Yang. He placed forty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yang Yingdong, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, and served as Instructor in the county school of Shangshui, Henan. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry, was first in birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Fu; his father, Xin; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His wife was née Yi. He ranked seventeenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Hanxiang, courtesy name Rusheng, was registered in a civilian household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry, was third in birth order, and was aged thirty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maosheng; his grandfather, Gao; and his father, Ying. His father's principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Mao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Han'ao and Hanju. His wife was née Shi. He ranked ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jiang, courtesy name Rugong, was registered in a guardsman household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and was a native of Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Record of Rites. He was third in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Lin; and his father, Jin, Vice Director of the Palace Crafts Service. His father's former wife was née Lü, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Huai and Pei, the latter Vice Director of the Palace Crafts Service; his younger brothers were Chun, also Vice Director of the Palace Crafts Service, and Lian. His wife was née Xu; he subsequently married women née Gao and née Zhan. He ranked fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yongzhen, courtesy name Zizhou, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes, was third in birth order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ru, a student of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather was Fen, posthumously awarded the titles Gentleman for Rendering Service and Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works; and his father was Zuanzong, a County Magistrate. His mother was née Qiao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yongbin, Yongguan, Meirui, Meizhu, Meixue, Meida, Meifu, and Meijia; his younger brothers were Yongzhang, Yongxing, Yongkang, and Yongyu. His wife was née Fan. He ranked thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Bin 蔣彬, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), in a civilian household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Gao; his father, Fang; and his mother, née Deng. Both parents were living. His elder brother Mao was a National University student; his younger brothers were Fan 樊, Fan 梵, and Sen, the last a National University student. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Yang 湯仰, courtesy name Zishan, was registered at Xindu Postal Relay Station, Chengdu Rear Guard, Sichuan, in an official household. An added student of the Xindu County school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Gan, grandfather Qin, and father Pinshen were all company commanders. His legal mother was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Qian. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ren, a company commander; Fu, a district magistrate; and Shi. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Shu 黃樞, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Yinghong and grandfather Zizhen both held honorary official rank conferred for longevity. His father was Xi, and his mother was née Ru. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Xiong. He placed twenty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Xiuke 盧修可, courtesy name Ziji, was registered in Xu Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a military household. A subprefectural school student, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi. His grandfather Yuan was an annual tribute student, posthumously appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His father Fu was a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father's former wife, née Zhao, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother, née Zheng, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother Jike was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his younger brothers were Shike and Dangke. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Sizhong, registered in a salt-producing household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Junheng; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the thirtieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yunneng, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Rujie; his father was Yijian; and his mother was née Fan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yunjiao, Daishan (an official awaiting selection for appointment), Wanzhong, Zheng, Junda, and Weilin [the division of the names Zheng and Junda is uncertain]. His wife was née Ye. He ranked thirty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Song, registered in a civilian household in Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenqing; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the nineteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather was Xian; his father was Zongzhe; his mother was née Xin; and his stepmother was née Tan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Baiqiao. His wife was née Zheng, and his subsequent wife was née Shi. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Hongzhen was registered in a military household in Xuanhua County, Nanning Prefecture, Guangxi, and was originally from Yuancheng County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). He was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingyu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather was Chengfang; his father was Ang, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hongguan and Hongfan, and his wife was née Chen. He ranked first in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lu, registered in a civilian household in Yifeng County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhaohe; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Lun, an Instructor posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master of the Palace and acting Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his grandfather was Yuanming, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, promoted to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his father was Li, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Lei. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were You, Zhan, Jie, and Shang. His wife was née Liu, and his subsequent wife was née Guo. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yue Xiang 岳相, of a military household registered in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an additional student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weizhong; he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, his grandfather Jiang, and his father Lian; his father's former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Cao. His father was deceased and his mother living; his wife was née Feng. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Guangxian 郜光先, of a civilian household registered in Changzhi County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi, was an additional student of the prefectural Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zixiao; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-seven years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather Lu, his father Qin, and his mother née Mi. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Jiang, his younger brother Guanglü, and his wife née Zhang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Menglin 邵夢麟, of a civilian household registered in Chuzhou, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daozheng; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Liang〔Prefectural School Instructor〕, and his father Tingxiang〔County School Instructor〕; his father's former wife was née Lu, his mother née Zhu, and his stepmother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Mengzhu, and his wife née Lu. He placed twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xun 朱纁, of a military household registered in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xuanfu; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was forty-three years old, and was born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Qian, his father Chuan, and his mother née Jia. Both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Kuang 絋, Ting 綎, Shen 紳, and Jin 縉, and his wife was née Song. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yan Congjian, registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongke; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty, born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yin芳 (Yinfang); his grandfather, Cui, was a magistrate; his father, Ning, was Director of Ceremonial; and his mother was née Tao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Congjie, an Imperial University student, and Congqian; his younger brothers were Congya, Congyu, Cong’ai, and Congxun. His wife was née Lu. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Qing, registered in a civilian household in Hezhou, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Huai, his grandfather Boyu, his father Jin, and his mother née Lu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Yang. He placed 105th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Ding was registered in a military household in Pinggu County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and came originally from Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ruji, ranked first in his family, and was aged thirty, born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Kai, had been granted the titles Grand Master for Consultative Service and Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Shen, was a county school instructor; his father, Ying, was a Ceremonial Usher; and his mother was née Hao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Cai, Xian (an honorary official), Zhou (a tribute student), Shou, and Guan; his younger brothers were Kuan, Yu, Shi, Yan, and Zi [?]. His wife was née Liu. He placed eighty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Zhili, registered in a civilian household in Yongchang Guard under the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission, was a guard school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruli; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-one, born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Jinghua, was a tribute student; his father, Yue, was a Steward; and his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Xing, registered in a civilian household in Dongming County, Daming Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Gongchen; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-three years old, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi Wenzeng, his grandfather Shi Neng, and his father Shi Kui; his mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shi Yu, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed 120th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yubi, registered in a civilian household in Quzhou County, Guangping Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zina; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen Quan, his grandfather Chen Sixiao, and his father Chen Shanli; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chen Yujie, and his wife was née Gu. He placed 35th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Chengneng, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zijing; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng Yu, an honorary official; his grandfather was Feng Du, a Stationmaster; and his father was Feng Deqian. Two mothers are listed, née Luo and née Ding. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Feng Chengming and Feng Chengwei, and his wife was née Qian. He placed 40th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Xun, registered in a military household in Shangqiu County, Guide Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bojing; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Song Gui, his grandfather Song Jin, and his father Song Ni; his mother was née Jin, and his stepmothers were née Guo and née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Song Zhao and Song Xu, and his wife was née Zhu. He placed 50th in the Henan Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Chengxuan, courtesy name Junqing, was registered in Yanjin County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Jing, was an Adjudicator; his father was Zi, and his mother was née Song. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Bian. He placed seventy-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Ziyi, courtesy name Ruyu, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a salt-producing household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather, Gui, was a prefectural Registrar; his father was Fan, and his mother was née Xie. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ziyu, and his younger brothers were Ziji, Ziqi, Zikui 蘷, Zilong, Zikui 夔, Ziyue, and Zitai. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed forty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zongdai, courtesy name Bodong, was registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather, Zhi, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father, Xu, was a School Instructor. His legal mother was née Niu, and his birth mother was née Ru. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Lü. He placed seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yaode, courtesy name Xingfu, was registered in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gao; his grandfather, Quan, was a subprefectural Clerk; his father, Yiqing, was a Station Master. His mother was née Bai, and his stepmother was née Dong. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉庠〔貫錦衣衛校籍，湖廣承天府鍾祥縣人，府學生，治詩經，字養吾，行一，年四十，十一月二十七日生〕。曾祖敬，祖倫，父廣，母武氏。永感下，弟序，娶陳氏，繼娶馬氏。湖廣鄉試第七十三名，會試第二百三十五名。

沈桐〔貫浙江湖州府歸安縣民籍，烏程縣人，縣學生，治春秋，字時秀，行二，年二十九，四月十三日生〕。曾祖操，祖珎，父霽，前母嚴氏，母凌氏。慈侍下，兄科，弟秩、穆，娶嚴氏。浙江鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百三十二名。

高文薦〔貫四川成都右衛軍籍，陝西鳳翔府鳳翔縣人，成都府學增廣生，治書經，字伯簡，行二，年三十三，二月二十日生〕。曾祖政，祖仕魁，父鵬，母周氏。慈侍下，兄文佐〔監生〕，弟文佑、文舉、文進、文選，娶何氏。四川鄉試第五十七名，會試第八十九名。
translation_en:
Cen Yongbin, registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yunmu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Wenkai held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather Zi likewise held an honorary longevity title and was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites; his father Wan was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Luo, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yongxiao, Yongzhong, Yongming, Yongan, Yongshou, Yongcheng, Yongyang, Yongxian, Yongcao, Yongjie, Yongtui, Yongchong, and Yonghui, and he married a woman née Xian. He placed eleventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xiang, registered in a guardsman's household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Zhongxiang County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yangwu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Lun, his father Guang, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Xu; he married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed seventy-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Tong, registered in a civilian household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Wucheng County, was a county government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shixiu, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Cao, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Ji; his father's former wife was née Yan, and his mother was née Ling. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Ke, his younger brothers were Zhi and Mu, and he married a woman née Yan. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Wenjian, registered in a military household of the Chengdu Right Guard in Sichuan and a native of Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an additional student of the Chengdu Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Bojian, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Shikui, his father Peng, and his mother née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Wenzuo was a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Wenyou, Wenju, Wenjin, and Wenxuan, and he married a woman née He. He placed fifty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

史嗣元〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字懋宗，行一，年二十九，十月二十日生〕。曾祖鳳〔封應天府經歷〕，祖伯敏〔州同知〕，父重光，母朱氏。具慶下，弟嗣亨、嗣泰、嗣憲，娶張氏。浙江鄉試第十八名，會試第五十五名。
translation_en:
Gu Jian 顧堅, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changshu County. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather You, and his father Lin; his mother was née Wei and his stepmother née Xu. His father was still living. His younger brothers were Yixue [?; the division of these names is uncertain], Yin, Shan, Kai, and Zhong. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Tan. He placed thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shundao 林舜道, courtesy name Yunzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a native of Huai'an County. Instructor at the Pingdu Department school in Shandong, he specialized in the Book of Changes, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhu, his grandfather Cong, and his father Yongxin; his mother was née Chen. His father was still living. His elder brother was Shunzhi, and his younger brothers were Shunju and Shunyang. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Yijing 歐陽一敬, courtesy name Sizhi, was registered in a military household in Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Chaozuo, his grandfather Yaoshan, who held an honorary official title for longevity, and his father Shu; his mother was née Bi. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Song. He placed fifty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Siyuan 史嗣元, courtesy name Maozong, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student at the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Feng, who was honorifically invested as Registrar of Yingtian Prefecture; his grandfather was Bomin, a Department Vice Magistrate; and his father was Chongguang. His mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Siheng, Sitai, and Sixian. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈人种〔貫直隸蘇州府嘉定縣民籍，縣學生，治《易經》，字時雍，行二，年二十九，十月初一日生〕。曾祖朴，祖祺，父球，前母朱氏、蔡氏，母薛氏。嚴侍下，兄人和，娶侯氏。應天府鄉試第一百六名，會試第二百二十八名。

林朝聘〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍，府學生，治《禮記》，字君珍，行二，年三十五，正月十五日生〕。曾祖椿，祖一能〔封知縣，加封戶部員外郎〕，父繼顯〔知州〕，母陳氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，弟騰〔總旗〕、朝臣、朝璇、朝亨、朝軾、朝瞻、朝紳、朝珊、朝宣、朝會，娶潘氏。福建鄉試第十三名，會試第一百二十五名。

蔣三益〔貫四川成都前衛官籍，陝西咸寧縣人，成都府學生，治《春秋》，字子謙，行二，年三十四，二月初七日生〕。曾祖鑑〔贈南京右軍都督府經歷〕，祖弼〔知府〕，父芹〔貢士〕，母曹氏。慈侍下，兄鵬〔千戶〕、三近〔百戶〕、三省，弟三畏、三餘、三祝、三樂，娶戴氏。四川鄉試第四十七名，會試第一百二十二名。
translation_en:
Peng Wenzhi, courtesy name Zaifen, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and served as Instructor at the county school of Yi County in Zhili. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bangyan, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Fu, an Education Intendant holding the rank of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his father was Dazhi, a Prefect. His father's principal wife, née Zhu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his stepmother, née Lin, was granted the same title; and his birth mother was née Song. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Wenyang, Wenxing, and Wenzhi 文陟; his younger brother was Wensheng. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Gu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Renzhong, courtesy name Shiyong, was registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Changes, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather Qi, and his father Qiu. His father's former wives were née Zhu and née Cai; his mother was née Xue. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Renhe, and he married a woman née Hou. He placed 106th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Chaopin, courtesy name Junzhen, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Record of Rites, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Yineng, granted the title of District Magistrate and subsequently that of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Jixian, a Department Magistrate. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title Lady. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Teng, a Company Commander, and Chaochen, Chaoxuan, Chaoheng, Chaos hi [Chaoshi], Chaozhan, Chaoshen, Chaoshan, Chaoxuan 朝宣, and Chaohui. He married a woman née Pan. He placed thirteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Sanyi, courtesy name Ziqian, was registered in an officer household of the Chengdu Front Guard in Sichuan, was originally from Xianning County in Shaanxi, and was a student of the Chengdu prefectural school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, posthumously granted the title of Registrar in the Nanjing Chief Military Commission of the Right; his grandfather was Bi, a Prefect; and his father was Qin, a tribute scholar. His mother was née Cao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Peng, a Chiliarch, Sanjin, a Centurion, and Sanxing; his younger brothers were Sanwei, Sanyu, Sanzhu, and Sanle. He married a woman née Dai. He placed forty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tian Dengnian, courtesy name Zideng, was registered in a civilian household in Zhongzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the department school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Xiang; his father, Yi, a Steward of Food; and his mother, née Ren. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Youqiu and his younger brother, Younian. He married a woman née Li and subsequently another woman née Li. He ranked ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huo Yuxia, courtesy name Mianzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Houyi, and grandfather, Hua, were each posthumously granted the titles of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites. His father, Tao, held those titles and received the posthumous name Wenmin. His father's principal wife, née Ou, was posthumously granted the title of Lady; his stepmother, née Zheng, was granted the title of Lady; and his birth mother was née Lü. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother, Yuqiu, was a Registry Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission. His younger brothers were Yumin, Yubin, Yuying (a tribute student), Yudeng, and Yuchang. He married a woman née Gan. He ranked ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yuan, courtesy name Zhongshen, was registered in a civilian household in Guangchang County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was fourth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huitong; his grandfather, Feng; his father, Qian; his mother, née Huang; and his stepmother, née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rui; his younger brothers were Tao (a tribute student), Hang (a tribute student), Wan, Mi, Huan, and Hu. He married a woman née Lai and subsequently a woman née Wei. He ranked eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Minde, courtesy name Xunshi, was registered in a civilian household in Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shoujing; his grandfather, Zijie; his father, Shi; his mother, née Liu; and his stepmother, née Liang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Minqiu. He married a woman née Liao and subsequently women née Liu, Deng, and Zhu. He ranked second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Luo Huangshang, courtesy name Meizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Gaoming County, Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked second in his family, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Jing, his father Zhen, and his mother née Tan; his father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Yi, and his younger brothers were Fang (a sacrificial official, shengjiguan), Huangjuan, and Huangzhong. His wife was née Ou. He placed sixty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yungui, courtesy name Junfang, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian; he was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked third in his family, and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun’an, his grandfather Mingong, his father Kuanchu, and his mother née Wang; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yuntong and his younger brother Yunmei. His wife was née Cai. He placed thirty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shan, courtesy name Keyu, was registered in a military household of the Runing Guarding Battalion in Henan; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first in his family, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingxian, his grandfather Youzhi, his father Yin, and his mother née Yan; both parents were living. His wife was née Lai, and he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed fortieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Junshang, courtesy name Rumao, was registered in a military household in Zichuan County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong; he was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked third in his family, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Chun, and his father Hui; his father’s former wife was née Jia, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Junxi, Junci, and Junyang; his younger brothers were Junchong, Zaiyang, Junpin, Tingyang, and Junming. His wife was née Zhou. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wei Shiliang, courtesy name Shunqing, was registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked eighth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengwu; his grandfather, Shangzhao, held an honorary longevity title; his father, Tianxiang, was a provincial sacrificial official; and his mother was née Tu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shiyan, Fu, Yue, Xian, Hong, and Shiyu. He married a woman née Wan. He placed fifty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Daonan, courtesy name Zongshi, was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked sixth in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Han; his father, Qiao; and his mother, née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Shangzhong and Shangzhi; his younger brothers were Daoning, Daolong, Daojie, and Daoquan. He married a woman née Weng. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Chuwang, courtesy name Silu, was registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Wenming; his father, Zhi; and his mother, née Wei. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chucai. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed sixtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Daji, courtesy name Rusu, was registered in a physician household under the Imperial Medical Institute and came from Yuhang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student of the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather, Zi, was a Vice Commissioner of a granary; and his father, Yuan, was an Imperial Physician. His father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Zheng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Dajing and Dabang. He was betrothed to a woman née Gao. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李轍〔貫陝西鳳翔府鳳翔縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字從道，行二，年三十二，八月初三日生〕。曾祖鍾，祖仲仁，父栢，母姚氏。永感下，兄輅，弟軏，娶白氏，繼娶强氏。陝西鄉試第二十四名，會試第一百八十六名。
