translation_en:
Zhu Bingru, courtesy name Zhongnan, was registered in an official household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Guiyang County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather, Hu; and his father, Xixian, a tribute scholar. His mother was née Jiang, and his stepmother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Yueru and Weiru, and his wife was née Liu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Zishou, courtesy name Bohua, was registered in an artisan household in Chiping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, a Granary Commissioner; his grandfather, Xuan, a Station Master; and his father, Hu. His mother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zixing and Zihou, and his younger brothers Ziwu, Ziqian, and Zimu. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eighteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhe, courtesy name Congdao, was registered in a civilian household in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Zhongren; and his father, Bai. His mother was née Yao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Lu, and his younger brother Yue. His wife was née Bai, and he subsequently married a woman née Qiang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Teng, courtesy name Wenqi, was registered in a civilian household in Wuning County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked tenth in birth order and was aged forty, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Changgui; his grandfather, Zhongluan, and his father, Ji, both held honorary official titles conferred for longevity. His mother was née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ji and Fen. His wife was née Wang, and he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Yue 徐鉞 was from Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in an artisan household, and an附生 supplementary student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yongxi. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Wenkai, his grandfather Tairong, and his father Kongsu; his mother was née Jiang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zheng. He married a woman née Zou and subsequently women née Bao and Mao. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Guangdian 程光甸 was from Taihu County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a commoner household, and a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziji. Ninth in birth order, he was aged forty-one and was born on the thirtieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather Lun and father Shaoyi were both District Magistrates. His father's former wife was née Lü, and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Guangshi; his younger brothers were Guangwan, Guangye (an Imperial University student), and Guangshu. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Qiming 何起鳴 was from Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, registered in a commoner household, and a supplementary student at the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yingqi. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xue, his grandfather Zongyi, and his father Xiang (a tribute scholar, gongshi); his mother was née Yang. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Qianming and Luanming. He married a woman née Tang. He ranked thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xiang 朱湘 was from Yiwu County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a commoner household, and an added student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziqing. Sixty-eighth in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather Qiong, and his father Hong; his mother was née Zong and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ting, Jing, and Ying [?]; his younger brothers were Song and Bian. He married a woman née Zheng. He ranked fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cao Dong, registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Longqing, and he ranked twentieth among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty years old, born on the eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ning; his grandfather, Gui, held honorary office for philanthropy; and his father, Yi, was a Ceremonial Usher. His principal mother was née Wu, his stepmother née Wang, and his birth mother née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Chun, Tong, Mu [?], Yu, Zhen (an Imperial University student), Di, Bai (an Imperial University student), Dong, and Yang; his younger brother was Cai. He married a woman née Guan. He placed ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Qiu, registered in Qiyang County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yingming, and he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-three years old, born on the sixteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Siyi, his grandfather Wo, his father Dasen, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ce and Shu. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Mingchun, registered in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zhaoyuan, and he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Zhen, held honorary office for philanthropy; and his father, Yu, was an Imperial University student. His principal mother and birth mother were both née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Mingxia. He married a woman née Huang. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Wei, registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Huanfu, and he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins. He was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Youcai; his grandfather, Yu, held honorary office for longevity; his father, Li, was a Sacrificial Attendant (shengjiguan); and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shou, Na, Si [?], Li, Ji, and Hui. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bao Daguan, courtesy name Juzhi, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ming was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather Ze was an Investigating Censor; and his father was Qi. His father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Fang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Daguang, and his younger brothers were Dachan, Dating, and Dajiong. He married a woman née Bao. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yongqing, courtesy name Shanfu, was registered in a military household of the Standard-Bearer Office of the Ceremonial Guard Office in Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youcai, his grandfather An, his father Chaoyu, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were still living. His elder brothers were Yongcheng, Yongqing, Yongshou, and Yongji. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed seventy-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Jie, courtesy name Mianfu, was registered in Wen'an County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, in a civilian household. A county government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Heng was a Guard Registrar, posthumously appointed Right Administrator; his grandfather Hong was a Right Administrator; and his father Chang was a Left Provincial Administration Commissioner. His mother, née Ma, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father alone was still living. His elder brother Yan was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his younger brother was Jin. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fen, courtesy name Shixin, was registered in Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather Xiao, his father Zipeng, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were still living. He married a woman née Cao. He placed 119th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Jun, courtesy name Zhefu, was registered in an official household of Liuzhou Guard, Guangxi, and was a native of Hefei County in the directly administered region. A student of the Maping County school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Yue, his father Song, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cheng, and his wife was née Dai. He placed thirty-third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ling, courtesy name Ruqi, was registered in a civilian household in Xingtai County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Huai, his father Xian, his mother née Shen, and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Quan and Yue, the latter an annual tribute student; his younger brother was Jian. His wife was née Zhu, and his subsequent wife née Zhang. He placed 111th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Lianggui, courtesy name Rusi, was registered in a military household of Shenwu Left Guard and was a native of Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Fu and grandfather Neng were both company commanders; his father was Shou, and his mother née Shao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Liangyu, Liangchen, and Liangxiang; his younger brothers were Liangcai and Liangqing. His wife was née Liang, and his subsequent wife née Shi. He placed eighty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yue Shunbin, courtesy name Zongyao, was registered in a salt-producing household in Dinghai County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twentieth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Youzhong, his grandfather Guishi, his father Zao, his mother née Zheng, and his stepmother née Hong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shunwei, and his wife was née Lin. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Yuncheng, courtesy name Rudeng, was registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Shuntian prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the eighteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Xian; and his father was Zichun. His mother was née Bao, and his stepmother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Pengcheng, and his wife was née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Fengqi, courtesy name Mingzhi, was registered in a commoner household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather was Qiong; and his father was Zhen. His mother was née Mo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Fenghe. His wife was née Chu; he subsequently married a woman née Yao. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Yihuai, courtesy name Jingming, was registered in a commoner household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mikai, a Postmaster; his grandfather was Cong, who held an honorary title for longevity (shouguan); and his father was Gui. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yichun, Yiqiu, and Yigui, and his wife was née Lin. He placed seventy-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Huiyou, courtesy name Tiangao, was registered in a commoner household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chongqin; his grandfather was Ruizhen; and his father was Huan. His mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Huiyan; his younger brothers were Huimo, Huidian, Huiyin, Huiqian, and Huizhao. His wife was née Cai. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Dong, registered in Wannian County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Gongyu; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shichang; his grandfather, En, was a School Instructor; his father was Huan, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Gan, and his wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Qiyuan, registered in Luancheng County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tiren; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xin, was a School Instructor; his grandfather was Luan; his father was Shiyong, and his mother was née Cheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yun, and his wife was née Hu. He placed seventy-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lou Rushan, registered in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Gong’an; he ranked 192nd in birth order within his lineage, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhaocheng, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Bin; his father was 𤇍 [reading uncertain], and his mother was née He. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Rukun and Ruxian, and his wife was née Lu. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ai, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tiren; he ranked first in birth order, was aged forty-three, and was born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding; his grandfather was Pin; his father, Pu, was a District Magistrate. His father’s former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Xiang and subsequently a woman née He. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yifu, courtesy name Zhenfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Yu, his father Xiang, and his mother née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Youfu and Zhongfu, and his wife was née Xing. He ranked eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Sijin, courtesy name Zhongmian, was registered in a civilian household in Ju Subprefecture, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Yuan, his father Bangli, and his mother née Hao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Sixue, a County Registrar, and Siwen; his wife was née Mao. He ranked sixty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenxu, courtesy name Deyan, was registered in a civilian household in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. A supplementary student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boxun, a Chief Clerk; his grandfather was Benxiong, an annual tribute student; his father was Kui, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Wenchun, Wengang, Wenwei, Wenqi, and Wenjing; his wife was née Zhou. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Weiji, courtesy name Ruqia, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Juchang, his grandfather Zhongyin, his father Mingluan, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Shen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Weilun, Weizhou, and Weishi; his younger brothers were Weizai and Weilian. His wife was née Jiang, and he subsequently married a woman née Mao. He ranked fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mei Weihe, registered in a military household of Puding Guard, Guizhou, was originally from Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the guard school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yuanchen; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the thirtieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Zhong was a Pacification Officer; his grandfather was Ji; and his father Yue was a Prefect. His father’s former wife was née Shen, and his mother was née Zhan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Weiyong, Weitiao, Weishi, Weishi (惟詩), and Weigeng. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yue, registered in a civilian household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruzong; he ranked fifth in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Shize was a Prefect; his grandfather was Lai; his father was Heng; and his mother was née Cai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun and Youde, and his younger brothers were Xing, Kai, Feng, and Chi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Ge, registered in a civilian household of Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county-school student and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Junzheng; he ranked third in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Chang was a School Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works; his grandfather Zhang held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Man; and his mother was née Yao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Gao, a Battalion Commander; Shu, an Imperial University student; and Zhuo (桌 [?]), an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Xin, Office Manager in the Chief Military Commission of the Left Army; Li, an Imperial University student; Biao; Jia; and Fang. He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shimao, registered in a military household of Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from Kunshan County. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingmei; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Lu was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of War in Nanjing. His grandfather Zhuo held those same titles. His father Shu was Supreme Commander of Military Affairs and Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, concurrently Left Vice Minister of War. His mother, née Yu, was granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shifang, Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant; Shide, Registrar of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent; Shiye, Translator in the Translators Institute; Shizhen, Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission; Shi’an; and Shiwang. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Jiamo, registered in a civilian household in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chengqing; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twentieth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingjing, his grandfather Gongyu, and his father Jie, a prefectural Registrar. His father’s former wife was née Xiao, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guanbao (ranked first in the first class of the Palace Examination), Guanxiang, Guanshi, Guanqiu, and Guannian; his younger brothers were Guanbian and Jiamou. His wife was née Luo. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Tianlu, registered in a military household of the Baoding Rear Guard in Zhili and a native of Dingxing County, was a student at the school of the Daning Regional Military Commission, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zixue; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyuan, his grandfather Ben, and his father Jin, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions. His father’s former wives were née Tian and née Wei, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Anyi; his younger brothers were Yin, Zuo, and Di. His wife was née Wang. He ranked twenty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Tingluo [?], registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Taicang Subprefecture, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shimin; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jizhao, his grandfather Lun, and his father Tai. His legal mother was née Mao, and his birth mother was née Ling. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His wife was née Lu. He ranked sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shen, registered in a civilian household in Changyuan County, Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiyin; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather Ming was granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel. His father Hu was Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Master of the Palace. His mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zhuang, Su, and Wan. His wife was née Cui. He ranked third in the Provincial Examination of □ Prefecture [name illegible] and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李輔〔貫江西南昌府進賢縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字子卿，行四，年二十九，六月二十日生〕。曾祖萼，祖廷裕，父柯，母陳氏。具慶下，兄軾，弟輿、載，娶齊氏，繼娶許氏。江西鄉試第五十五名，會試第八名。

龐瀾〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字觀吾，行一，年三十六，四月初一日生〕。曾祖質，祖璟〔壽官〕，父欽，母許氏。嚴侍下，娶潘氏。順天府鄉試第一百二名，會試第二百七十七名。

李琦〔貫光禄寺厨籍，直隸常州府江陰縣人，順天府學附學生，治書經，字伯玉，行一，年二十五，十月二十三日生〕。曾祖昂，祖安〔壽官〕，父錄〔典膳〕，母王氏。具慶下，弟珍、珎，娶朱氏。順天府鄉試第八十名，會試第二百八十六名。
translation_en:
Xie Tingjie 謝廷傑 was registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zongsheng, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yikui, Minister of Works, posthumously awarded the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wenzhuang; his grandfather was Ji 緝, honorarily appointed Administrative Assistant of Yingtian Prefecture; his father was Ji 驥, Administrative Assistant of Yingtian Prefecture; his father's principal wife, Lady Wan, was posthumously awarded the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother, Lady Zhang, was awarded the same title; and his birth mother was Lady Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Tingxian, Tinghe, Tinglan, Tingyou, and Tingjun, his younger brothers were Tingju and Tingqian, and his wife was Lady Ouyang. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Fu 李輔 was registered in a civilian household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ziqing, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was E, his grandfather Tingyu, his father Ke, and his mother Lady Chen. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Shi, his younger brothers were Yu and Zai, and he married Lady Qi and subsequently Lady Xu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pang Lan 龐瀾 was registered in a military household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guanwu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Jing held an honorary official title granted for longevity, his father was Qin, and his mother Lady Xu. His father was living and his mother deceased; his wife was Lady Pan. He placed 102nd in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qi 李琦 was registered in a cook household attached to the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was a native of Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili; he was a supplementary student at the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, his courtesy name was Boyu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ang, his grandfather An held an honorary official title granted for longevity, his father Lu was a Steward (dianshan), and his mother was Lady Wang. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Zhen 珍 and Zhen 珎, and his wife was Lady Zhu. He placed eightieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cai Xi 蔡悉, registered in an artisan household in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shijie; he ranked fourth in birth order and was twenty-four years old, born on the third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Yin, and his father Tingyong; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mao (a tribute student), Yu, Zhong, Si, Xian, and Shu, and his younger brothers were Zhi, De, Si, Nian, Yi, and Qing [division of the brothers’ names uncertain]. His wife was née Sun. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jieling 劉介齡, registered in a commoner household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaoxiu; he ranked fifth in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yue, his grandfather Yi, and his father Chen; his father’s former wife was née Luo, and his mother was née Pan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shangji and Shangjiong. His wife was née Shao. He placed sixty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jia 張檟, registered in a commoner household in Xincheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shuyang; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Weide and grandfather Tingyong both held honorary official status for charitable contributions; his father was Hui, and his mother was née Shangguan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dong (an Imperial University student) and Qi; his younger brother was An. His wife was née Xiao. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Fengxiang 戴鳳翔, registered in a salt-producing household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and a native of Jiaxing County, was an supplementary student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhizeng; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Shineng, his grandfather Wenshen, and his father Guan; his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fenglai and Fengyi; his younger brothers were Fengming and Fengcai. His wife was née Zhou. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Jiaochuan, registered in a military household in Chaocheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rufan; he ranked third in birth order, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Long, and his father Laipin; his mother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Xingchuan and Daochuan, and his younger brothers Zhongchuan, Xinchuan, Zhengchuan, and Jingchuan. He married a woman née Tian. He placed fifty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhai Tai, registered in a civilian household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Siping; he ranked sixth in birth order, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Fu, and his father Kun. His father's former wife was née Tang, his mother née Wan, and his stepmother née Sheng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Fa, You, Zuo, Shi (an annual tribute student), and Cheng; his younger brothers were Qi, Yi, Xun, Zao, and Hui. He married a woman née Cao. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jin, registered in an artisan household in Zhucheng County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an added-quota student at the county school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruwen; he ranked second in birth order, was thirty-one years old, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Xian, and his father Fan. His father's former wife was née Hou, and his mother née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wei, Yong, Shen (a sacrificial official, shengji guan), and Ze; his younger brother was Zhou. He married a woman née Fan. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Mingyi, registered in an artisan household in Le'an County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xizheng; he ranked second in birth order, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong. His grandfather Yu was a County Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father Shen was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Jiang, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren), and his stepmother, née Cui, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Mingluo, and his younger brothers were Mingnan and Minggao. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖逢慶〔教授〕　祖埴〔訓導〕　父惟〔縣丞〕　前母李氏　母張氏　繼母朱氏

治易經字汝宜行一年四十九月初六日生
曾祖靖〔同知〕　祖廷賢　父賜　母陳氏
重慶下　弟桂　楙　娶陳氏
福建鄉試第六十二名　會試第一百六十三名
punctuated:
梁梧〔貫河南汝寧府信陽衛，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字鳳鳴，行一，年三十二，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖安，祖孜，父瀛，母杜氏。具慶下，弟檟、樞，娶潘氏。河南鄉試第十名，會試第一百二十九名。

邢邦〔貫山東東昌府臨清州，民籍，國子生，治易經，字維翰，行一，年四十，二月二十三日生〕。曾祖琛〔壽官〕，祖畯〔典史〕，父秉仁〔進士〕，母干氏，繼母解氏。永感下，弟邠、郇，娶王氏。山東鄉試第四十七名，會試第二百七十四名。

蔣凌漢〔貫四川成都府金堂縣，民籍，華陽縣學生，治易經，字節甫，行一，年三十七，八月十一日生〕。曾祖逢慶〔教授〕，祖填〔訓導〕，父惟繇，前母李氏，母張氏，繼母朱氏。嚴侍下，娶張氏。四川鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百二名。

詹彬〔貫福建泉州府安溪縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝宜，行一，年四十，九月初六日生〕。曾祖靖〔州同知〕，祖廷賢，父賜，母陳氏。重慶下，弟桂、楙，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第六十二名，會試第一百六十三名。
translation_en:
Liang Wu, registered with Xinyang Guard in Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Fengming. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Zi, his father Ying, and his mother née Du. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jia and Shu, and his wife was née Pan. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Bang, registered in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Weihan. First in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the twenty-third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather Jun was an unranked secretary; and his father Bingren was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi). His mother was née Gan and his stepmother née Xie. His parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Bin and Xun, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Linghan, registered in Jintang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Huayang County school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Jiefu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Fengqing was a professor, his grandfather Tian an assistant instructor, and his father Weiyou. His father's former wife was née Li, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Zhu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Bin, registered in Anxi County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruyi. First in birth order, he was aged forty and was born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jing was a subprefect; his grandfather was Tingxian, his father Ci, and his mother née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Gui and Mao, and his wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫汝翼 貫順天府密雲縣民籍 國子生
治書經字舜臣行一年二十九七月初九日生
曾祖海 祖寬 父塡〔知縣〕 母祝氏
具慶下 弟汝爲汝礪汝明汝聽 娶楊氏繼娶秦氏鄭氏

punctuated:
熊秉元〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字仁卿，行六，年二十二，六月十三日生〕。曾祖伯用，祖斯佑，父顧，母李氏。嚴侍下，弟秉貞，娶余氏，繼娶徐氏。江西鄉試第九十三名，會試第二百四名。

丘達道〔貫四川成都府綿州，民籍，儒士，治書經，字和仲，行八，年二十四，六月十八日生〕。曾祖友成，祖應祖〔典史〕，父岳〔知縣〕，母胡氏。慈侍下，兄志道、大道、載道、從道、弘道、學道、信道，弟明道，娶戴氏。四川鄉試第四十八名，會試第四十三名。

平康裕〔貫直隸保定府新城縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字德遠，行二，年二十九，八月二十五日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖洪〔省祭官〕，父旦〔歲貢生〕，母范氏。具慶下，兄康祚，弟康祈、康衢、康祐、康祜，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第五十八名，會試第六十六名。

孫汝翼〔貫順天府密雲縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字舜臣，行一，年二十九，七月初九日生〕。曾祖海，祖寬，父填〔知縣〕，母祝氏。具慶下，弟汝為、汝礪、汝明、汝聴，娶楊氏，繼娶杜氏、鄭氏。順天府鄉試第八十七名，會試第一百四十九名。
translation_en:
Xiong Bingyuan, courtesy name Renqing, was registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An附 student (supplementary student) of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Boyong; his grandfather, Siyou; his father, Gu; and his mother, née Li. His father alone was living. His younger brother was Bingzhen. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Xu. He ranked ninety-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Dadao, courtesy name Hezhong, was registered in Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents, he was eighth in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Youcheng; his grandfather, Yingzu, a County Clerk; his father, Yue, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née Hu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhidao, Dadao, Zaidao, Congdao, Hongdao, Xuedao, and Xindao; his younger brother was Mingdao. He married a woman née Dai. He ranked forty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ping Kangyu, courtesy name Deyuan, was registered in Xincheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Hong, a Sacrificial Official; his father, Dan, an annual tribute student; and his mother, née Fan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kangzu; his younger brothers were Kangqi, Kangqu, Kangyou, and Kanghu. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Ruyi, courtesy name Shunchen, was registered in Miyun County, Shuntian Prefecture, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather, Kuan; his father, Tian, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ruwei, Ruli, Ruming, and Ruting. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently women née Du and née Zheng. He ranked eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄

慈侍下兄經緯〔知縣〕娶趙氏
山西鄉試第二十七名會試第一百九名
張齊〔貫陝西西安府長安縣民籍國子生治禮記字子修行五年二十八十月十七日生〕
曾祖穟祖鏗〔貢士〕父棟〔監生〕嫡母盧氏生母薛氏

曾祖會　祖文曉　父崑　母李氏

punctuated:
王緝〔貫山西汾州衛官籍，直隸鳳陽府定遠縣人，國子生，治書經，字熙甫，行三，年三十四，三月初五日生〕。曾祖謙〔百戶〕，祖瑄〔百戶〕，父鶴，母張氏。慈侍下，兄經、緯〔知縣〕，娶趙氏。山西鄉試第二十七名，會試第一百九名。

張齊〔貫陝西西安府長安縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字子修，行五，年二十八，十月十七日生〕。曾祖穟，祖鏗〔貢士〕，父棟〔監生〕，嫡母盧氏，生母薛氏。具慶下，兄褒、亮、扆，弟表，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第五名，會試第二百八十四名。

顧廷對〔貫直隸揚州府泰州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字子俞，行二，年三十，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖行〔府經歷〕，祖𤣱〔縣丞〕，父雲鳳〔知縣〕，母徐氏。重慶下，兄廷問，弟廷謂、廷策、廷幹、廷論，娶宋氏。應天府鄉試第六名，會試第九十一名。

朱擢〔貫陝西西安府渭南縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字登庸，行一，年三十二，正月十七日生〕。曾祖會，祖文曉，父崑，母李氏。慈侍下，弟採、捷、接、按，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第八名，會試第二百九十二名。
translation_en:
Wang Ji, courtesy name Xifu, was registered in an officer household of Fenzhou Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Qian and grandfather Xuan were company commanders; his father was He and his mother was née Zhang, with his mother alone surviving; his elder brothers were Jing and Wei, the latter a county magistrate, and his wife was née Zhao; he placed twenty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qi, courtesy name Zixiu, was registered in a civilian household in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sui, his grandfather Keng was a tribute student, and his father Dong was an Imperial University student; his father's principal wife was née Lu and his birth mother was née Xue, and both parents were living; his elder brothers were Bao, Liang, and Yi, his younger brother was Biao, and his wife was née Wang; he placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Tingdui, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a civilian household in Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xing was a prefectural registrar, his grandfather, whose name is transcribed as 𤣱 [?], was an assistant magistrate, his father Yunfeng was a county magistrate, and his mother was née Xu; he had living grandparents and parents, his elder brother was Tingwen, his younger brothers were Tingwei, Tingce, Tinggan, and Tinglun, and his wife was née Song; he placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zhuo, courtesy name Dengyong, was registered in a civilian household in Weinan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi; a student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather was Wenxiao, his father was Kun, and his mother was née Li, with his mother alone surviving; his younger brothers were Cai, Jie (捷), Jie (接), and An, and his wife was née Wang; he placed eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄

賈淇〔貫河南河南府嵩縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字希武，行三，年三十六，十一月初七日生〕。曾祖膺，祖宗，父錫，母王氏。具慶下，兄濂、漁，弟沐、澄、洛、渭，娶王氏，繼娶髙氏。河南鄉試第七十三名，會試第一百十三名。

尹約〔貫山東兗州府平陰縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字一之，行一，年三十，正月初九日生〕。曾祖彝〔府通判〕，祖惟能〔縣丞〕，父獻可，母李氏。慈侍下，弟緒、紹、紳，娶趙氏。山東鄉試第五十三名，會試第二百七十一名。

周鳴塤〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄水縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字思友，行一，年四十二，七月二十二日生〕。曾祖仕淮，祖紹武〔縣丞〕，父楫〔縣丞〕，嫡母毛氏，生母梅氏。永感下，兄鳴鎬〔監生〕，弟鳴篪〔監生〕、鳴鸝、鳴陽、鳴春、鳴咸、鳴琚、鳴濩、鳴堰、鳴雷，娶夏氏，繼娶毛氏。湖廣鄉試第五十一名，會試第三十四名。
translation_en:
Wu Yushi, courtesy name Yixing, was registered in a salt-producing household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a native of Rong County, Jiading Subprefecture. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tang; his grandfather, Keyi; his father, Zhun; his mother, née Jiang; and his stepmother, née Wei. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Yuli and Yule, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Qi, courtesy name Xiwu, was registered in a civilian household in Song County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked third in family birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Zong; his father, Xi; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lian and Yu; his younger brothers were Mu, Cheng, Luo, and Wei. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Gao. He placed seventy-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Yue, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Pingyin County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, a prefectural assistant prefect; his grandfather, Weineng, a county vice magistrate; his father, Xianke; and his mother, née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Xu, Shao, and Shen, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed fifty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Mingxun, courtesy name Siyou, was registered in a civilian household in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An added student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shihuai; his grandfather, Shaowu, a county vice magistrate; and his father, Ji, also a county vice magistrate. His legal mother was née Mao, and his birth mother was née Mei. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Minggao, a student of the Imperial University; his younger brothers were Mingchi, also a student of the Imperial University, Mingli, Mingyang, Mingchun, Mingxian, Mingju, Minghu, Mingyan, and Minglei. He married a woman née Xia and subsequently a woman née Mao. He placed fifty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃儀〔貫廣東廣州府東莞縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字象卿，行三，年二十九，三月初八日生〕。曾祖祖蔭，祖銘，父玥，母陳氏。具慶下，兄偉、諫〔監生〕，弟仰，娶黎氏。廣東鄉試第五十六名，會試第三十七名。

趙訥〔貫山西汾州孝義縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字孟敏，行二，年三十九，六月二十五日生〕。曾祖泰〔縣主簿〕，祖鴻〔壽官〕，父思商〔縣主簿〕，母田氏。具慶下，兄時曉，弟時讃、暘，娶宋氏，繼娶李氏。山西鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百十七名。

張希稷〔貫山東青州府高苑縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字于田，行二，年三十七，七月十六日生〕。曾祖士舉，祖盤，父珝，前母陳氏，母崔氏。永感下，兄希尹，弟希龍、希召〔貢士〕，娶楊氏。山東鄉試第四十二名，會試第二百九十名。
translation_en:
Yu Yan, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Congzhong, ranked nineteenth in family order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Huan; and his father, Jian. His father's former wife was Lady Jin, and his mother was Lady Wu; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zichong (a subprefectural administrative assistant), Zixiang, and Wen; his younger brother was Liangyin. He married Lady Shen. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yi, registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Xiangqing, ranked third in family order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuyin; his grandfather, Ming; his father, Yue; and his mother, Lady Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wei and Jian (an Imperial University student), and his younger brother was Yang. He married Lady Li. He placed fifty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Ne, registered in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Mengmin, ranked second in family order, and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai (a county registrar); his grandfather, Hong (holder of an honorary title for longevity); his father, Sishang (a county registrar); and his mother, Lady Tian. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shixiao, and his younger brothers were Shizan and Yang. He married Lady Song and subsequently Lady Li. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xiji, registered in Gaoyuan County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Yutian, ranked second in family order, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiju; his grandfather, Pan; and his father, Xu. His father's former wife was Lady Chen, and his mother was Lady Cui; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xiyin, and his younger brothers were Xilong and Xizhao (a tribute scholar, gongshi). He married Lady Yang. He placed forty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

馮珊〔貫直隸真定府藁城縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字仲鳴，行一，年三十二，十月二十八日生〕。曾祖選，祖世隆，父守之，前母王氏，母張氏。慈侍下，弟瑚，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第四十五名，會試第二百四十九名。

鄭惟僑〔貫湖廣荆州府石首縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字子愛，行一，年四十，六月二十日生〕。曾祖懋，祖文昕〔縣丞〕，父璧，母管氏。慈侍下，弟惟和、惟中、惟寅、惟吉，娶謝氏。湖廣鄉試第八十七名，會試第二百九十四名。
translation_en:
Hong Youdi 洪有第 was registered in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Maoxue and ranked first in birth order; he was twenty-seven, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, an Honorary Official for Righteousness; his grandfather was Zhou; his father was Tingshi, a Prefectural Vice Prefect; and his mother was née Zhang. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Youheng, Yourong (a tribute scholar), and Youfei; his younger brothers were Youfu, Youlin, Youyan, Yousheng, Youjie, and Youdu. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventy-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Guangzu 孫光祖 was registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zishao and ranked twenty-second in birth order; he was thirty-one, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xi, granted the title of Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather was Lian, Chief Case Reviewer in that court; his father was Xin; and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chengzu, Xijie, and Jingzu. His wife was née Yu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shan 馮珊 was registered in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zhongming and ranked first in birth order; he was thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Shilong; his father was Shouzhi; his father’s former wife was née Wang; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was still living. His younger brother was Hu, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Weiqiao 鄭惟僑 was registered in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zi’ai and ranked first in birth order; he was forty, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao; his grandfather was Wenxin, a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Bi; and his mother was née Guan. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Weihe, Weizhong, Weiyin, and Weiji. His wife was née Xie. He placed eighty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Dahua 高大化, courtesy name Shaoxian, was registered in a commoner household in Yishui County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four [?; the transcription has 生 in place of the expected 年], and born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Mu; his grandfather, Fu, held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Qian, and his mother was née Dou. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother, Datong, was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Daxun, Dagao, Dadao, and Daye. His wife was née Wang. He ranked thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Zongyi 鮑宗沂, courtesy name Zhitong, was registered in a commoner household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jingxian; his grandfather, Rong; his father, Qing; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Zongsi, and his wife was née Zhu. He ranked seventieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhen Jin 甄津, courtesy name Ruwen, was registered in an official household in Yutai County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather, Heng, held an honorary title for righteousness; his father, Kai, was a county Registrar; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Pu, Pang, Pan, Bian (an Imperial University student), and Pei (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort). His wife was née Liu. He ranked twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Yong 夏永, courtesy name Jifu, was registered in an official household in Guangning Qiantun Guard, Liaodong. A guard school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Xian; his father, Jingming, was a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Kang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Chang, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Dai 孫代, registered in Fufeng County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Shaofu; he ranked fifth in the family, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Wan, and his father Shu; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were You, Jia, Wei, and Ren, and his younger brother was Shi. His wife was née Liu. He placed fifteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Mei 周美, registered in Fuyang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zichong; he ranked twenty-seventh in the family, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Yi, and his father Ke; his mother was née Zhao and his stepmother née Hua. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ao; his younger brothers were Xie (an Imperial University student), Xuan, Xun, Yao, Gao, and Lian. His wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xiangyang 李向陽, registered in Yazhou, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongqing; he ranked second in the family, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Feng, and his father Yin. His father's former wives were née Chen and née Li; his mother was née Ma and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chaoyang. His wife was née Cao; he subsequently married a woman née Mu. He placed fiftieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Daqi 羅大玘, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weijie; he ranked first in the family, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuye, his grandfather Jiuhuan, and his father Gongshen; his mother was née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Dazuo, Dacai (an annual tribute student), Fu (an Investigating Censor), Dazhen, and Daluan. His wife was née Long. He placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Jia, registered in the Rear Battalion of the Central Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yiqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youliang, his grandfather Qin, and his father Cen, a School Instructor; his mother and stepmother were both née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ke, Di, and Dengfeng. He married a woman née Qi. He placed 108th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Yiren, registered in Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Chun, and his father Lin; his mother was née Chen. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Yixin. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed forty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Kongwen, registered in Dazu County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhiqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hanxiao, his grandfather Shouling, and his father Xun; his mother was née Yan and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Kongzhang and Kongmo. He married a woman née Liao and subsequently women née Wang and née Xiao. He placed forty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shu, registered in Yangcheng County, Zezhou Subprefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunqing; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Kemei, and his father Jie; his mother was née Ru. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhi, a tribute scholar, and Dong. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李承嗣〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字貞立，行三十五，年三十三，正月初六日生〕。曾祖鼎〔贈工部右侍郎〕，祖傑〔義官〕，父維翰〔陰陽正術〕，母傅氏。永感下。兄承宣，弟承訓、承寀、承家、承守。娶王氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十一名，會試第二百二十四名。

張庸〔貫河南汝寧府光州光山縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字子登，行五，年三十二，四月十一日生〕。曾祖道清，祖璲〔知縣〕，父如軫，前母胡氏，母舒氏。慈侍下。兄應〔知縣〕、康、庚、慶，弟庶、席。娶謝氏。河南鄉試第十六名，會試第二百二十七名。

侯峩〔貫山西潞安府長治縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子謙，行三，年三十三，正月二十九日生〕。曾祖廣，祖璉，父方，母崔氏。具慶下。兄崇、嵐，弟峴、巍、嵐、屭，從岑、崋。娶仇氏。山西鄉試第五十名，會試第一百五十六名。
translation_en:
Wang Tingzhan, registered in a military household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhibiao; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Simin, a Vice Prefect; his grandfather was Wenkui, posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Rites; and his father was Ji, Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His legal mother was née Wang, granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his birth mother was née Xu. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tingru, Administrative Assistant of Shuntian Prefecture, and Tingchen, formerly a Hanlin Bachelor; his younger brothers were Tingyang and Tingqian, both students of the Directorate of Education, and Tingdi. He married née Chen and subsequently née Mao. He placed sixty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengsi, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenli; he ranked thirty-fifth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ding, posthumously appointed Right Vice Minister of Works; his grandfather was Jie, an honorary official for charitable contributions; and his father was Weihan, an astrological official (yinyang zhengshu). His mother was née Fu. His parents were deceased. His elder brother was Chengxuan; his younger brothers were Chengxun, Chengcai, Chengjia, and Chengshou. He married née Wang. He placed 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yong, registered in a civilian household in Guangshan County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zideng; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Daoqing; his grandfather was Sui, a Magistrate; and his father was Ruzhen. His father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Shu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Ying, a Magistrate, Kang, Geng, and Qing; his younger brothers were Shu and Xi. He married née Xie. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou E, registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather was Lian, and his father was Fang; his mother was née Cui. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chong and Lan; his younger brothers were Xian, Wei, Lan [?], and Xi; his paternal cousins were Cen and Hua. He married née Qiu. He placed fiftieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Jin 張縉 was registered in a civilian household in Anyang County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zizhong; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Zuo, and his father Caiguang; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Chang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun, and Ji; his younger brothers were Shen, Gang (a tribute scholar), and Wei. He married a woman née Shen. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Bideng 侯必登 was registered in a military household of Guangxi Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture. He was a student of the Chengjiang prefectural school specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Maoxue; he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, his grandfather Yongcheng, and his father Anguo (an honorary official honored for longevity); his mother was née Yang. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Bizhong, Bifeng, Bichong, and Bixian; his younger brother was Biqin. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Ji. He ranked second in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Nanjin 劉南金 was registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and was an attached student of the Xiangfu county school specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Xianqing; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding, his grandfather Yaoyin, and his father Kan; his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were still living. He married a woman née Li. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhenzhi 張振之 was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongqi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jifang, his grandfather Jie, and his father Shitang; his mother was née Yu. His father alone was still living. His elder brother was Fuzhi. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked sixty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

周弘祖〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字元孝，行二，年三十一，九月十四日生〕。曾祖洙〔知縣，贈監察御史〕，祖廷徵〔按察司副使，進階中憲大夫〕，父鋮〔縣丞〕，母汪氏。具慶下，兄〔弘迪，貢士〕，弟〔弘禮、弘吉、弘止、弘祚、弘甫、弘掄、弘祐、弘袷、弘示、弘享、弘祈、弘祁、弘祉、弘袠、弘裕〕，娶余氏。湖廣鄉試第六十九名，會試第四十九名。

馬文學〔貫直隸保定府雄縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字行先，行一，年四十，四月初六日生〕。曾祖珎〔監生〕，祖隆，父智，母高氏，繼母高氏。慈侍下，弟文奇，娶韓氏。順天府鄉試第一百五名，會試第二百三十一名。
translation_en:
Zhang Yundao 張蘊道, courtesy name Junpin, was registered in a civilian household in Ningxiang County, Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xian, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Ao, an honorary official for righteousness; his father was Wen; his mother was née Wu, and his stepmother née Wang. His father alone was still living. His younger brother was Yunxue, and his wife was née Shi. He placed thirty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Dalun 郭大綸, courtesy name Zili, was registered as a guardsman in the Embroidered-uniform Guard and came from Boxing County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Tong, and his father Tai; his father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Mu. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Dajing, his younger brother Daben, and his wife née Wang. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Hongzu 周弘祖, courtesy name Yuanxiao, was registered in a civilian household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhu, a District Magistrate posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Tingzheng, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner promoted in prestige rank to Grand Master for Constitutional Service; his father was Cheng, a Vice Magistrate; and his mother was née Wang 汪. Both parents were living. His elder brother Hongdi was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Hongli, Hongji, Hongzhi 弘止, Hongzuo, Hongfu, Honglun, Hongyou, Hongjia, Hongshi, Hongxiang, Hongqi 弘祈, Hongqi 弘祁, Hongzhi 弘祉, Hongzhi 弘袠, and Hongyu. His wife was née Yu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Wenxue 馬文學, courtesy name Xingxian, was registered in a civilian household in Xiong County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Long, his father Zhi, his mother née Gao, and his stepmother also née Gao. His father was deceased, and his mother or stepmother was still living. His younger brother was Wenqi, and his wife was née Han. He placed one hundred fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.
