translation_en:
Wu Fengchun, courtesy name Zimu, was registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chengqian; his grandfather, Rong; his father, Leidong; and his mother, née Zheng. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Fengji and his younger brother Fengtai; his wife was née Cai. He placed forty-first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Ru, courtesy name Shuchun, was registered in a military household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An added student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jizhou, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Tai; his father, Zhong; and his mother, née Lin. His father alone was still living. His younger brothers were Jie and Shi; his wife was née Tang. He placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Chaozong, courtesy name Yuhai, was registered in a civilian household in Chaoyi County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Jingxin; his father, Kui; his mother, née Yang; and his stepmother, née Ma. His father alone was still living. His younger brother was Chaoji. He married a woman née Ma and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed thirteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xu, courtesy name Yuanqing, was registered in a military household of the Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Xinghua County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Dengzhou prefectural Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather, Ying; his father, Ang, a student of the Imperial University; and his mother, née Chen. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Ao, a prefectural Investigator; 𦐥 [name reading uncertain]; and Yi, a Steward. His younger brother was He, and his wife was née Chen. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:

棄之夫大學之道
專以用人理財為
急用得其人政自
治財理得宜用自
===

而代理之責豈我
獨能耶茲欲聞人
得用財得理以至
治美刑平華尊夷

言之者後盡背而

專以用人理財爲

治財理得宜用自
===
足吁人之不我用
而代理之責豈我
獨能耶兹欲閑人

translation_en: …what they had spoken of, they later wholly repudiated and abandoned. The Way of the Great Learning gives particular urgency to employing men and managing finances. I now wish to hear how men may be properly employed and finances properly managed, so that government may flourish, punishments be equitable, the Chinese realm be honored, and the non-Chinese peoples …

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
臣丁士美
臣對臣聞帝王之致治也必君臣交儆而後
可以底德業之成必人臣自靖而後可以盡
代理之責何者天地之大德曰生而其所欲
生者莫甚于民故立之君以理之是君也者
承天之命者也當以天之心為心者也聖人
之大寶曰位而所以守位者莫要于得民故
設之臣以分理之是臣也者承君之命者也
當以君之心為心者也君以天之心為心則
有純天之心有憲天之政宗子之責盡矣臣
===
===
以君之心為心則事君如事天事君如事親
冢相之責塞矣是知君責任乎臣臣責難於
君是謂交儆交相得而益章泰道之所以成
也志存乎立功事專乎報主是謂自靖君得
臣而化行理道之所以永也然則一心一德
君臣固當共成其休而自靖自獻人臣又可
不自盡其心也哉帝王所以禮樂明備而天
地官刑政肅清而民人服蒞中國而內順治
撫四夷而外威嚴者胥此交儆之誠自靖之
誼有以致之也恭惟

撫四夷而外威嚴者胥此交儆之誠自靖之

punctuated:
臣丁士美

臣對：臣聞帝王之致治也，必君臣交儆而後可以底德業之成，必人臣自靖而後可以盡代理之責。何者？天地之大德曰生，而其所欲生者莫甚于民，故立之君以理之。是君也者，承天之命者也，當以天之心為心者也。聖人之大寶曰位，而所以守位者莫要于得民，故設之臣以分理之。是臣也者，承君之命者也，當以君之心為心者也。君以天之心為心，則有純天之心，有憲天之政，宗子之責盡矣。臣以君之心為心，則事君如事天，事君如事親，冢相之責塞矣。是知君責任乎臣，臣責難於君，是謂交儆。交相得而益章，泰道之所以成也。志存乎立功，事專乎報主，是謂自靖。君得臣而化行，理道之所以永也。然則一心一德，君臣固當共成其休，而自靖自獻，人臣又可不自盡其心也哉？帝王所以禮樂明備而天地官，刑政肅清而民人服，蒞中國而內順治，撫四夷而外威嚴者，胥此交儆之誠、自靖之誼有以致之也。恭惟
translation_en:
Your servant, Ding Shimei.

Your servant replies: I have heard that, for emperors and kings to bring about good government, ruler and ministers must admonish one another before they can bring their virtue and achievements to fruition; ministers must conscientiously fulfill their own duties before they can discharge their responsibility for governing on the ruler’s behalf. Why is this? The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life, and among those whose lives they wish to sustain, none are more important than the people. Thus a ruler is established to govern them. The ruler receives Heaven’s mandate and should take Heaven’s heart as his own. The sage’s great treasure is called the throne, and nothing is more essential to preserving the throne than winning the people. Thus ministers are appointed to share in governing them. Ministers receive the ruler’s commands and should take the ruler’s heart as their own. When the ruler takes Heaven’s heart as his own, his heart accords wholly with Heaven and his government follows Heaven’s example: his responsibility as Heaven’s eldest son is fulfilled. When ministers take the ruler’s heart as their own, they serve him as they serve Heaven and as they serve their parents: their responsibility as chief ministers is discharged.

From this we know that the ruler holds ministers responsible for their duties, while ministers call upon the ruler to accomplish what is difficult. This is called mutual admonition. Through their mutual accord, each becomes more illustrious; this is how harmonious government is achieved. To set one’s aspirations on meritorious achievement and devote one’s service entirely to repaying one’s lord is called conscientiously fulfilling one’s own duties. When the ruler obtains worthy ministers, his transforming influence takes effect; this is how good government endures. Thus ruler and ministers should surely be united in heart and virtue, together bringing their good work to completion. Yet in conscientiously fulfilling their duties and offering themselves in service, how could ministers fail to devote their hearts to the utmost?

That emperors and kings make rites and music manifest and complete, so that Heaven and Earth perform their proper functions; that they make punishments and government orderly and pure, so that the people submit; that they preside over the Central Kingdom with obedience and order within, and pacify the peoples of the four quarters with awe-inspiring authority abroad—all this is brought about through sincerity in mutual admonition and a sense of duty in conscientiously fulfilling one’s responsibilities. I respectfully consider…

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝陛下禀剛健中正之資合天地陰陽之德際
中興極治之會成
明聖作述之能至道超于元始而靈貺昭祥精
誠格于
重玄而休徵協應德教洋溢于域中威聲振揚于
海外嘉靖萬邦迄今三十又八載矣臣竊伏
草茅霑被
治化何幸囿於天覆地載之中而游於鳶飛魚
躍之境也乃今
萬幾之暇進臣等于
===

…Your Majesty the Emperor, endowed with strength, vigor, balance, and rectitude, unites in yourself the virtues of Heaven and Earth, yin and yang. At this juncture of dynastic resurgence and consummate governance, you have fulfilled the capacity of enlightened sages both to create and to carry forward their predecessors’ work. Your supreme Way surpasses the primordial beginning, and divine blessings manifest auspicious signs; your utmost sincerity reaches the highest heavens, and favorable portents respond in accord. Your virtuous instruction overflows throughout the realm, and your awe-inspiring renown resounds beyond the seas. You have brought harmony and peace to the myriad states, now for thirty-eight years. Your servant, dwelling humbly among the common people, has received the benefits of your transforming rule. How fortunate I am to live beneath Heaven’s shelter and upon Earth’s sustaining ground, and to roam in a world where kites soar and fish leap!

text:
以直遂也於是即億兆之中擇夫聰明之□
者而畀之以統乎華夷之位焉是君也者上
焉而有奉天之責也子道繫焉敢不敬與下
焉而有字民之責也父道繫焉可不勤與天
之與民其理一也敬之與勤其撰一也故明
此于二帝其道隆矣然必曰欽若昊天必曰
敬授人時也必曰勅天之命必曰食哉惟時
也明此于三王其治烈矣然必曰昭受上帝
必曰下民昏墊也必曰顧諟明命必曰子惠
困窮也必曰亦臨亦保必曰卑服即功也必
===
曰恭天成命必曰大賚四海也若是者何居
君道則然也故君必敬天勤民而後爲克君
臣又聞之書曰明王奉若天道建邦設都樹
后王君公承以大夫師長不惟逸豫惟以治
民禮曰惟王建國辨方正位體國經野設官
分職以爲民極蓋言君有父母斯民之心而
不能以自遂也於是即類聚之中擇夫才賢
之備者而與之以共理民物之責焉是臣也
者上焉而有代終之義也爲上爲德敢或欺
與下焉而有長民之寄也爲下爲民可或害

之與民其理一也敬之與勤其揆一也故明

者上焉而有代終之義也為上為德敢或欺
與下焉而有長民之寄也為下為民可或害
punctuated:
以直遂也。於是，即億兆之中，擇夫聰明之□者，而畀之以統乎華夷之位焉。是君也者，上焉而有奉天之責也，子道繫焉，敢不敬與？下焉而有字民之責也，父道繫焉，可不勤與？天之與民，其理一也；敬之與勤，其撰一也。故明此于二帝，其道隆矣。然必曰「欽若昊天」，必曰「敬授人時」也；必曰「勅天之命」，必曰「食哉惟時」也。明此于三王，其治烈矣。然必曰「昭受上帝」，必曰「下民昏墊」也；必曰「顧諟明命」，必曰「子惠困窮」也；必曰「亦臨亦保」，必曰「卑服即功」也；必曰「恭天成命」，必曰「大賚四海」也。若是者何居？君道則然也。故君必敬天勤民，而後爲克君。
臣又聞之，《書》曰：「明王奉若天道，建邦設都，樹后王君公，承以大夫師長，不惟逸豫，惟以治民。」《禮》曰：「惟王建國，辨方正位，體國經野，設官分職，以爲民極。」蓋言君有父母斯民之心，而不能以自遂也。於是，即類聚之中，擇夫才賢之備者，而與之以共理民物之責焉。是臣也者，上焉而有代終之義也，爲上爲德，敢或欺與？下焉而有長民之寄也，爲下爲民，可或害
translation_en:
…bring this intention directly to fulfillment. Thus, from among the countless multitudes, Heaven selects someone whose intelligence is [?] and grants him the position of ruling over the Chinese and the non-Chinese peoples. As ruler, he bears responsibility above for serving Heaven: the duties of a son attach to him—dare he fail to be reverent? Below, he bears responsibility for nurturing the people: the duties of a father attach to him—can he fail to be diligent? Heaven and the people are united in principle; reverence and diligence are united in purpose. The Two Emperors understood this, and their Way was exalted. Yet it was necessary to say both, “Reverently accord with august Heaven,” and, “Reverently communicate to the people the seasons for their labors”; both, “Attend carefully to Heaven’s mandate,” and, “Food! Attend to it at the proper time.” The Three Kings understood this, and their achievements in government were illustrious. Yet it was necessary to say both, “Illustriously receive the charge of the Lord on High,” and, “The people below were overwhelmed and submerged”; both, “Keep constantly in view this bright mandate,” and, “Show parental kindness to those in distress and poverty”; both, “Watch over them and protect them,” and, “Wear humble clothing and devote oneself to the work”; both, “Reverently obey Heaven’s settled mandate,” and, “Bestow generous gifts throughout the Four Seas.” Why was this so? Such is the Way of the ruler. Thus a ruler must revere Heaven and labor diligently for the people before he can fulfill his role as ruler.
Your servant has also heard these words from the Book of Documents: “The enlightened kings reverently followed Heaven’s Way, established states and capitals, appointed sovereigns, kings, rulers, and dukes, and supported them with grand masters and leaders—not for ease and pleasure, but to govern the people.” The Rites says: “When the king establishes the capital, he distinguishes the cardinal directions and fixes the proper positions, lays out the capital and divides the countryside, establishes offices and apportions duties, thereby providing a standard for the people.” This means that the ruler wishes to act as father and mother to the people but cannot fulfill that intention by himself. Thus, from among those gathered together, he selects men possessing both ability and worthiness and entrusts them with shared responsibility for governing the people and all things. As ministers, they have an obligation above to carry their ruler’s work through to completion: acting for their superior and for virtue, dare they practice any deception? Below, they are entrusted with leadership of the people: acting for those below and for the people, can they inflict any harm…

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
與君之于民其體一也忠君愛民其心一也
故明此于舜禹其績懋矣然必曰熈載亮工
必曰柔遠能邇也必曰過門不入必曰敷土
奠川也明此于稷契臯陶伊傅其職殫矣然
必曰樹藝五穀必曰敬敷五教也必曰思曰
賛襄必曰知人安民也必曰俾后堯舜必曰
時予之辜也必曰以匡乃辟必曰以康兆民
也若是者何居臣道則然也故臣必忠君愛
民而後為克臣三代而下英君誼辟代有作
者而昏迷而怠棄而狎侮而盤遊者不少也
===
名卿碩輔亦不乏人而誣上而蠹國而慢君
而賊民者比比也則知唐虞三代之所以久
安長治者非其氣數之適然也其君臣之交
修交省其人臣之自靖自獻者有以致之也
後世之所以不能有唐虞三代之治者亦非
其氣數之適然也其君臣之以逸以豫其人
臣之自私自利者有以致之也仰惟
陛下仁孝之德上通于天樂利之休磅礴于地
臨御以來
聖政之詳固不能以殫述而敬

translation_en:
…? The ruler and the people form one body; loyalty to the ruler and love for the people arise from one heart. Thus, when this principle was made manifest in Shun and Yu, their achievements were great. Yet of Shun it must be said that he “advanced undertakings and assisted in their accomplishment” and “cherished those far away and conciliated those nearby”; of Yu, that he “passed his own gate without entering” and “ordered the lands and settled the rivers.” When this principle was made manifest in Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue, they fulfilled their offices to the utmost. Yet of Ji it must be said that he “planted and cultivated the five grains”; of Xie, that he “reverently disseminated the five teachings”; and of Gao Yao, that he “deliberated and assisted” [?] and “discerned men’s abilities and brought peace to the people.” Of Yi Yin it must be said that he “made his sovereign a Yao or a Shun” and declared, “This is my fault”; of Fu Yue, that he acted “to correct your sovereign” and “to bring well-being to the myriad people.” Why was this so? Such is the way of a minister. Only through loyalty to his ruler and love for the people can a minister truly fulfill his role.
After the Three Dynasties, outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns arose in every age. Yet there were also many who were benighted, negligent, contemptuous, or engrossed in pleasure excursions. Nor was there any lack of eminent high ministers and great counselors; yet those who deceived their sovereigns, drained their states, slighted their rulers, and harmed the people were everywhere. We may therefore understand that the enduring peace and lasting good government of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties were no mere accident of their allotted destiny. They were brought about by rulers and ministers cultivating and examining themselves in concert, and by ministers conscientiously fulfilling their duties and offering their service. Likewise, the inability of later ages to attain the good government of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties was no mere accident of their allotted destiny. It was brought about by rulers and ministers indulging in ease and pleasure, and by ministers pursuing their own interests and advantage.
I reverently reflect that Your Majesty’s benevolence and filial devotion reach Heaven above, while the blessings of happiness and prosperity spread throughout the earth. Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, the particulars of your sagely government have indeed been too numerous to recount exhaustively; yet reverence …

text:
天勤民尤為先務之急者焉觀諸
欽天有記煥發昭事之忱
大報有歌丕揚祗答之敬以至因星變而
勅諭因水旱而責躬寅奉之心徹顯微而無間
其敬
天也何如其至也殆與堯之欽天舜之勅天禹之
昭受湯之自責文之臨保武之恭承一而已
矣
無逸有殿克念小民之依
豳風有亭昭示力本之教以至發
===
內帑以賑民窮減貢獻以節民力惠卹之念合
遐邇而皆然其勤民也何如其切也殆與堯
之如天舜之好生禹之盡力湯之子惠文之
如傷武之若保一而已矣然
陛下敬
天之心雖已至而臣之奉承
德意者每不能精白以承休
陛下勤民之心雖甚殷而臣之承流宣化者每不
能攄純以仰副其在
朝廷輦轂固必有竭忠秉義之臣矣而違上所

無逸有殿，克念小民之依；豳風有亭，昭示力本之教。以至發內帑以賑民窮，減貢獻以節民力，惠卹之念合遐邇而皆然。其勤民也，何如其切也！殆與堯之如天、舜之好生、禹之盡力、湯之子惠、文之如傷、武之若保，一而已矣。
然陛下敬天之心雖已至，而臣之奉承德意者，每不能精白以承休；陛下勤民之心雖甚殷，而臣之承流宣化者，每不能攄純以仰副。其在朝廷輦轂，固必有竭忠秉義之臣矣，而違上所
translation_en:
…Heaven and diligent care for the people are especially urgent among the foremost duties. Consider the Record of Revering Heaven (Qintian), which splendidly expresses the sincerity of your manifest service, and the Song of the Great Recompense (Dabao), which grandly proclaims your reverence in respectfully requiting Heaven. Furthermore, you issue admonitory edicts in response to celestial anomalies and reproach yourself in response to floods and droughts. Your reverent devotion extends without interruption through both the manifest and the hidden. How consummate is your reverence for Heaven! It is surely one with Yao’s reverence for Heaven, Shun’s heedfulness toward Heaven, Yu’s illustrious reception of its charge, Tang’s self-reproach, King Wen’s watchful protection, and King Wu’s reverent acceptance.
There is a Hall of No Idleness (Wuyi), where you keep in mind what the common people depend upon; there is a Pavilion of the Airs of Bin (Binfeng), which clearly displays the teaching that one must labor at agriculture, the fundamental occupation. Furthermore, you release funds from the imperial treasury to relieve the people’s poverty and reduce tribute offerings to spare their resources and labor. Your compassionate concern embraces those far and near alike. How earnest is your diligent care for the people! It is surely one with Yao’s Heaven-like benevolence, Shun’s love of life, Yu’s unstinting exertions, Tang’s kindness toward the people as his children, King Wen’s care for them as though they were injured, and King Wu’s care as though protecting an infant.
Yet although Your Majesty’s reverence for Heaven is already consummate, those ministers charged with carrying out your virtuous intentions often fail to receive your beneficence with purity of purpose. Although Your Majesty’s diligent concern for the people is most profound, those ministers charged with transmitting your influence and spreading your transforming instruction often fail to give full expression to their sincerity in fulfilling your wishes. At court, in the imperial capital, there must certainly be ministers who exhaust their loyalty and uphold righteousness; yet those who disobey what their sovereign…

也則曰吾不可以不得其情司空以掌邦土
也則曰吾不可以不興其利以沃君心以弼
君違而臺諫之自靖猶是也以阜成兆民以
惠養元元而藩臬之自靖猶是也大法小廉
百官修輔而自靖如一焉則人各無負于心
矣無負于心則有裨于民而能以君之心為
心矣是人臣之能自靖者始于一念之不欺
終于有孚之盈缶也其不能自靖者始之内
以欺于心終之上以負天子也有君如此寧
忍負之耶臣伏讀
===
聖制曰大學之道專以用人理財為急用得其人
政自治財理得宜用自足吁人之不我同而代
理之責豈我獨能耶臣以為天道不言而品物
亨歲功成者四時之吏五行之佐宣其氣也
君道不勞而庶績熙治功成者公孤論道六
卿率屬張其教也使舉代天理物之責而望
陛下以獨能是猶長養萬物甄陶萬類不必四時
之生成五氣之翕散而望於穆之天道以獨
運其化也不曰聖如堯舜而水土之平稼穡
之教必有賴於禹稷之賢五教之弼山澤之

text:
烈必有待於皐陶伯益之儔耶臣又伏讀
聖制曰兹欲聞人得用財得理以至治美刑平華
尊夷遁久安之計何道可臻且欲臣等有言之
必盡也臣竊以為用人有道務乎聰明之實
而已矣何謂聰明之實精其選嚴其課久其
任而已矣是故精擇于未用之先如其道德
經濟之兼優則雖沉淪草澤隆之大任可也
古有說築傅巖而爰立作相者矣慎察于既
用之後如其貪殘寵賂之用彰則必紏之重
罰勿狥其譽言可也古有烹阿大夫而齊國
===
大治者矣責成于考績之餘如其政蹟顯著
則增禄進秩勿移其地可也古有為京兆九
年者為郡守十年者或請久任或諫數易者
矣如是而人之不我用者未之有也理財有
道理其所以耗吾財者而已矣所謂理其耗
者去三浮汰三盈審三計而已矣是故官浮
于冗員也禄浮于冗食也用浮于冗費也此
之謂三浮去浮以存約曾鞏之說可舉也賞
盈于太濫也俗盈于太侈也利盈于太趨也
此之謂三盈酌盈以濟虛陸贄之說可舉也

punctuated:
烈，必有待於皐陶、伯益之儔耶？臣又伏讀聖制曰：「兹欲聞人得用、財得理，以至治美刑平、華尊夷遁、久安之計，何道可臻？」且欲臣等有言之必盡也。
臣竊以為，用人有道，務乎聰明之實而已矣。何謂聰明之實？精其選，嚴其課，久其任而已矣。是故精擇于未用之先，如其道德經濟之兼優，則雖沉淪草澤，隆之大任可也。古有說築傅巖而爰立作相者矣。慎察于既用之後，如其貪殘寵賂之用彰，則必紏之重罰，勿狥其譽言可也。古有烹阿大夫而齊國大治者矣。責成于考績之餘，如其政蹟顯著，則增禄進秩，勿移其地可也。古有為京兆九年者，為郡守十年者，或請久任，或諫數易者矣。如是而人之不我用者，未之有也。
理財有道，理其所以耗吾財者而已矣。所謂理其耗者，去三浮，汰三盈，審三計而已矣。是故官浮于冗員也，禄浮于冗食也，用浮于冗費也，此之謂三浮。去浮以存約，曾鞏之說可舉也。賞盈于太濫也，俗盈于太侈也，利盈于太趨也，此之謂三盈。酌盈以濟虛，陸贄之說可舉也。
translation_en:
…achievements necessarily depended upon men such as Gao Yao and Bo Yi, did they not? Your servant has also reverently read the imperial decree: “We now wish to hear by what means we may attain the proper employment of men and management of wealth, and thereby achieve excellent government, equitable punishments, the exaltation of the Chinese realm and the retreat of the foreign peoples, and lasting peace.” You further desire that we, your servants, fully express whatever we have to say.
Your servant humbly believes that the proper way to employ men consists simply in making discerning judgment effective. What does this mean? Simply to select them carefully, assess them rigorously, and retain them long in office. Thus, scrutinize candidates before employing them: if they excel both in moral character and in statecraft, even if they languish in rural obscurity, they may be elevated to great responsibilities. In antiquity, Yue was building walls at Fuyan when he was appointed chief minister. Examine men carefully after employing them: if their greed, cruelty, reliance on favor, and bribery become manifest, they must be subjected to severe punishment, without yielding to words spoken in their praise. In antiquity, the Grand Master of A was boiled to death, and the state of Qi became well governed. Demand results following performance evaluations: if officials have conspicuous administrative achievements, their stipends and ranks may be increased without transferring them elsewhere. In antiquity, some served as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao for nine years, and others as commandery governor for ten years; some requested prolonged tenure, while others remonstrated against frequent changes of officeholders. With such measures, there has never been a case in which men could not be put to our service.
The proper way to manage wealth consists simply in controlling what depletes our resources. To control such depletion means simply to eliminate the three superfluities, reduce the three excesses, and examine the three plans. Official establishments become excessive through redundant personnel; stipends, through supporting those who render no service; and expenditure, through unnecessary outlays. These are called the three superfluities. Zeng Gong’s proposal to eliminate superfluity and preserve frugality may be put into practice. Rewards become excessive through indiscriminate bestowal; customary practices, through extravagant luxury; and the pursuit of profit, through undue eagerness. These are called the three excesses. Lu Zhi’s proposal to draw upon surpluses to remedy deficiencies may be put into practice.

text:
有不終歲之計下也有數歲之計中也有萬
世之計上也是誠天不能使之災地不能使
之貧盜賊不能使之困蘇軾之上計可圖也
如是而財之不理者未之有也然此固用人
理財之方也所以求端用力之地臣請探本
盡言之焉孔子曰為政在人取人以身言純
心為用賢之本也
今日之用人亦曰在
陛下之居敬而已矣居敬則明通由是而照臨百
官將賢否不能淆邪正不能眩也居敬則公
溥由是而鼓舞群工將賞罰無所私彰癉無
所徇也以之而取賢歛才則皐夔稷契之在
列而善人為寶矣以之而黜伏庸回則共工
驩兜之放遠而不畜聚歛矣此又非用人之
大本乎伊尹曰慎乃儉德惟懷永圖言克儉
為君道之大也
今日之理財亦曰在
陛下之崇儉而已矣崇儉則後宮無曳地之衣由
是公卿勵楊綰之素勳戚有馬廖之風也崇
儉則一人惜露臺之費由是百官有羔羊之

有不終歲之計，下也；有數歲之計，中也；有萬世之計，上也。是誠天不能使之災，地不能使之貧，盜賊不能使之困，蘇軾之上計可圖也。如是而財之不理者，未之有也。然此固用人理財之方也，所以求端用力之地，臣請探本盡言之焉。
孔子曰：「為政在人，取人以身。」言純心為用賢之本也。今日之用人，亦曰在陛下之居敬而已矣。居敬則明通，由是而照臨百官，將賢否不能淆，邪正不能眩也；居敬則公溥，由是而鼓舞群工，將賞罰無所私，彰癉無所徇也。以之而取賢歛才，則皐夔稷契之在列，而善人為寶矣；以之而黜伏庸回，則共工驩兜之放遠，而不畜聚歛矣。此又非用人之大本乎？伊尹曰：「慎乃儉德，惟懷永圖。」言克儉為君道之大也。
今日之理財，亦曰在陛下之崇儉而已矣。崇儉則後宮無曳地之衣，由是公卿勵楊綰之素，勳戚有馬廖之風也；崇儉則一人惜露臺之費，由是百官有羔羊之
translation_en:
…There are plans that do not extend even to the end of a year: these are the lowest. There are plans for several years: these are intermediate. There are plans for ten thousand generations: these are the highest. Indeed, Heaven cannot bring disaster upon such a realm, Earth cannot impoverish it, and robbers cannot reduce it to distress: Su Shi’s highest plan can be pursued. With such measures, there has never been a case in which finances were not properly managed. Yet these are, to be sure, methods for employing men and managing wealth. As for finding the starting point at which to apply effort, your servant asks leave to examine the root and explain it fully.
Confucius said: “The conduct of government depends upon men; selecting men depends upon one’s own person.” This means that a pure heart is the foundation for employing the worthy. The employment of men today likewise depends simply upon Your Majesty’s abiding in reverence. Abiding in reverence brings clarity and discernment; with these you may scrutinize the hundred officials, so that the worthy and unworthy cannot be confused, nor the corrupt and upright mistaken for one another. Abiding in reverence brings impartiality and breadth; with these you may inspire all your officials, so that rewards and punishments admit no favoritism, and commendation and censure no partiality. By these means, selecting the worthy and gathering talent will bring men such as Gao, Kui, Ji, and Qi into the ranks of office, and good men will be treasured. By these means, dismissing and restraining the mediocre and perverse will send men such as Gonggong and Huandou into distant exile, and rapacious revenue collectors will not be retained. Is this not the great foundation for employing men? Yi Yin said: “Be mindful of your virtue of frugality, and cherish plans for the long term.” This means that the ability to practice frugality is a great principle of the ruler’s Way.
The management of wealth today likewise depends simply upon Your Majesty’s honoring frugality. If you honor frugality, there will be no robes trailing on the ground in the palace women’s quarters. Through this example, the highest ministers will strive to emulate Yang Wan’s simplicity, and meritorious nobles and imperial relatives will adopt Ma Liao’s manner. If you honor frugality, you, the sovereign, will begrudge the expense of a dew terrace; through this example, the hundred officials will possess the … of “Lamb’s Wool” …

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
節兆民有蟋蟀之儉也自是而開財之源則
生之者衆為之者疾而有財有用矣自是而
節財之流則食之者寡用之者舒而以財發
身矣此又非理財之大本乎本立則末治上
行則下效由是身帥天下而興讓興仁將治
日益美大畏民志而使民無訟將刑日益平
正是四國而中國治安將華日益尊蠻貊率
俾而守在四夷將夷日益遁由是而卜鼎于
億年由是而傳世于萬葉聖神功化之極久
安長治之方要在本原之地加之意焉而已
===
矣臣草茅狂瞽不識忌諱干冒
天威不勝戰慄隕越之至臣謹對

安長治之方要在本原之地加之意焉而已

punctuated:
節，兆民有蟋蟀之儉也。自是而開財之源，則生之者衆，為之者疾，而有財有用矣；自是而節財之流，則食之者寡，用之者舒，而以財發身矣。此又非理財之大本乎？本立則末治，上行則下效。由是身帥天下而興讓興仁，將治日益美；大畏民志而使民無訟，將刑日益平；正是四國而中國治安，將華日益尊；蠻貊率俾而守在四夷，將夷日益遁。由是而卜鼎于億年，由是而傳世于萬葉。聖神功化之極，久安長治之方，要在本原之地加之意焉而已矣。
臣草茅狂瞽，不識忌諱，干冒天威，不勝戰慄隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en:
…integrity, and the myriad people will practice the frugality commended in “The Cricket.” If, on this basis, the sources of wealth are opened, those who produce it will be numerous and those who work at it swift, so that there will be wealth and resources for use. If, on this basis, the outflow of wealth is restrained, those who consume it will be few and those who spend it measured, so that wealth will serve to cultivate one’s person. Is this not also the great foundation of managing wealth? Once the foundation is established, the particulars will be well ordered; when those above act, those below follow their example. Thus, by personally leading all under Heaven to cultivate deference and benevolence, Your Majesty’s governance will daily improve. By holding the people’s sentiments in great awe and bringing them to have no litigation, punishments will daily become more equitable. By setting the states of the four quarters aright and bringing order and peace to the Central Realm, the prestige of Chinese civilization will daily increase. As the Man and Mo peoples all submit, and the empire’s defense rests with the peoples of the four frontiers, foreign peoples will daily retreat farther away. Thus may the dynastic tripods be divined to endure for a hundred million years, and the dynasty be transmitted through ten thousand generations. The highest achievement of sagely and divine transformative rule, and the means to lasting peace and enduring order, depend above all on giving attention to these foundations.
Your servant, a rustic of rash and benighted understanding, ignorant of what must not be said, has presumptuously offended Your Majesty’s heavenly authority. I am overwhelmed by trembling and dread, as though about to fall and perish. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
臣毛惇元
臣對臣聞帝王之御天下也必治人與治法
兼舉而後可以弘其化於無窮必臣道與君
道交修而後可以善其法於不匱蓋法者經
國之紀人者植國之楨惟人與法常相資而
後立者也使有治法而無治人以經綸之則
補偏救敝之謨將有所滯而弗舉矣何以稱
民安物阜之休耶君者紀法之宗臣者紀法
之守惟君與臣常相須而有成者也使有聖
君而無賢佐以勵翼之則濟世安民之澤將
===
有所壅而弗流矣何以稱君明臣良之慶耶
然則主治於上者幾雖有萬而不必求之於
多術也惟人以立法法以經治本末兼舉而
四海雍熈之業自永保於無虞矣賛治於下
者分雖甚懸而不當飾之以虛文也惟忠以
立心心以事君上下相孚而一時喜起之猷
自交修於勿替矣由是康濟兆民則兆民蒙
其福由是震懾四夷則四夷賓其化由是垂
憲萬世則萬世仰其成此用人理財所以敷
為大學之訓而明良胥慶稱帝王之盛治者

憲萬世則萬世仰其成此用人理財所以數
為大學之訓而明良胥慶稱帝王之盛治者
punctuated:
臣毛惇元

臣對：臣聞帝王之御天下也，必治人與治法兼舉，而後可以弘其化於無窮；必臣道與君道交修，而後可以善其法於不匱。蓋法者經國之紀，人者植國之楨，惟人與法常相資而後立者也。使有治法而無治人以經綸之，則補偏救敝之謨將有所滯而弗舉矣，何以稱民安物阜之休耶？君者紀法之宗，臣者紀法之守，惟君與臣常相須而有成者也。使有聖君而無賢佐以勵翼之，則濟世安民之澤將有所壅而弗流矣，何以稱君明臣良之慶耶？

然則主治於上者，幾雖有萬，而不必求之於多術也。惟人以立法，法以經治，本末兼舉，而四海雍熈之業自永保於無虞矣。賛治於下者，分雖甚懸，而不當飾之以虛文也。惟忠以立心，心以事君，上下相孚，而一時喜起之猷自交修於勿替矣。由是康濟兆民，則兆民蒙其福；由是震懾四夷，則四夷賓其化；由是垂憲萬世，則萬世仰其成。此用人理財所以敷為大學之訓，而明良胥慶稱帝王之盛治者，
translation_en:
Your servant Mao Dunyuan.

Your servant replies: I have heard that, in governing all under Heaven, emperors and kings must employ both capable governors and sound methods of government before they can extend their transforming influence without limit. The duties of ministers and those of the ruler must be cultivated together before their institutions can be perfected and sustained without exhaustion. Institutions are the framework for ordering the state; men are the pillars that uphold it. Men and institutions can stand firm only through their constant mutual support. If sound institutions exist but there are no capable governors to administer them, plans to correct imbalances and remedy abuses will become obstructed and remain unimplemented. How, then, could one speak of the blessings of a people at peace and abundant resources? The ruler is the fountainhead of institutional order, and ministers are its custodians. Ruler and ministers can achieve success only through their constant reliance upon one another. If there is a sage ruler but no worthy assistants to encourage and support him, the beneficence that delivers the age from distress and brings peace to the people will be blocked and fail to flow forth. How, then, could one speak of the felicity of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers?

Thus, although the critical affairs confronting the ruler who directs government from above are myriad, he need not seek solutions through a multiplicity of techniques. Let men establish institutions and institutions order government: when root and branches are attended to together, the achievement of harmony and prosperity throughout the Four Seas will naturally be preserved forever, free from peril. Those who assist government from below, although their station is far removed from the ruler’s, should not embellish their service with empty formalities. Let loyalty establish the heart, and let that heart serve the ruler: when those above and below trust one another, the plans of an age in which ruler and ministers joyfully rouse one another to action will naturally be cultivated together without lapse. By these means, bring well-being and relief to the teeming people, and they will receive the blessings; overawe the barbarians of the four quarters, and they will submit to the transforming influence; bequeath exemplary standards to ten thousand generations, and those generations will look up to these accomplishments. This is why employing men and managing wealth were set forth as teachings in the Great Learning, and why an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoicing together have been acclaimed as the flourishing government of emperors and kings …

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
至今不衰也恭惟
皇帝陛下體
天地好生之心行聖賢大學之道寶善人如金玉
愛蒼生猶赤子君子和於朝小民和於野藹
藹乎親賢樂利之風近者無不悅遠者無不
來巍巍乎修齊治平之績是故上道揆而下
法守刑政肅清内順治而外威嚴華夷一統
雖古唐虞三代之治何以加茲乃猶
聖不自聖特進臣等于
廷而詢以用人理財之術久安長治之方甚盛
===
心也臣雖至愚無所知識然大學之訓則已
習聞之久矣敢不掇拾陳詞以對揚
休命於萬一乎甞聞之大學曰克配上帝言君之
尊猶上帝也又曰孝者所以事君言臣之事
君猶事親也夫君以配帝為尊則端拱穆清
其道常主於逸臣以移孝為忠則夔夔祗載
其道常主於勞使君而匪逸則以上帝而兼
行下土之職非所以為君矣臣而匪勞則以
厥子而不服厥父之事非所以為臣矣不觀
之天之生物乎長養庶類煦嫗群生者天之

punctuated:
至今不衰也。
恭惟皇帝陛下，體天地好生之心，行聖賢大學之道，寶善人如金玉，愛蒼生猶赤子。君子和於朝，小民和於野，藹藹乎親賢樂利之風；近者無不悅，遠者無不來，巍巍乎修齊治平之績。是故上道揆而下法守，刑政肅清；内順治而外威嚴，華夷一統。雖古唐虞三代之治，何以加茲？乃猶聖不自聖，特進臣等于廷，而詢以用人理財之術、久安長治之方，甚盛心也！
臣雖至愚，無所知識，然大學之訓，則已習聞之久矣。敢不掇拾陳詞，以對揚休命於萬一乎？甞聞之，《大學》曰：「克配上帝。」言君之尊猶上帝也。又曰：「孝者，所以事君。」言臣之事君猶事親也。夫君以配帝為尊，則端拱穆清，其道常主於逸；臣以移孝為忠，則夔夔祗載，其道常主於勞。使君而匪逸，則以上帝而兼行下土之職，非所以為君矣；臣而匪勞，則以厥子而不服厥父之事，非所以為臣矣。不觀之天之生物乎？長養庶類、煦嫗群生者，天之
translation_en:
…has remained undiminished to this day.
We reverently reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor embodies Heaven and Earth’s heart that cherishes life and practices the Way of the Great Learning taught by the sages and worthies. You treasure good men like gold and jade and love the common people like infants. Gentlemen live in harmony at court, and ordinary people live in harmony in the countryside: how abundant is the spirit of cherishing the worthy, enjoying happiness, and benefiting from good government! Those nearby are all delighted, and those afar all come to you: how lofty are your achievements in cultivating the self, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven! Thus those above judge affairs by the Way, while those below uphold the laws; punishments and administration are orderly and clear. Within, there is obedient and orderly government; beyond, there is awe of your authority. The Chinese and the foreign peoples are united under one rule. How could even the ancient governments of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties surpass this? Yet, though a sage, you do not regard yourself as one. You have specially summoned us, your servants, into court to inquire about methods of employing men and managing wealth, and means of securing lasting peace and enduring good government. How noble is your intention!
Though your servant is utterly foolish and without knowledge, I have long been familiar with the teachings of the Great Learning. How could I dare fail to gather established sayings and thereby respond to and extol even a ten-thousandth part of your gracious command? I have heard it said in the Great Learning: “He was able to match the Lord on High.” This means that the ruler’s exalted position is like that of the Lord on High. It also says: “Filial piety is that whereby one serves the ruler.” This means that a minister serves his ruler as he serves his parents. Since the ruler’s dignity lies in matching the Lord on High, he sits upright with folded hands in solemn purity, and his Way is always founded upon repose. Since the minister’s loyalty lies in transferring his filial devotion to his ruler, he reverently and cautiously undertakes his duties, and his Way is always founded upon toil. If the ruler does not enjoy repose, this would be like the Lord on High also performing the duties of the earth below: that is not the proper way to be a ruler. If a minister does not toil, this would be like a son failing to undertake his father’s business: that is not the proper way to be a minister. Have you not observed how Heaven brings forth living things? To nurture the myriad kinds and warm and cherish all living beings is Heaven’s…

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
心也而所以長養之煦嫗之者則惟日以暄
之雨以潤之風以噓之雷以震之而天不自
為也譬之巨室之治產凡大而耕穫織紝之
勞細而灑掃應對之役皆其子孫臣僕有以
分任而代為之而所謂嚴君者則惟總其綱
焉已爾聴其成焉已爾然則君臣之間又何
以異於是乎是故家視天下者則以君為宗
子臣為家相言宗子之事皆家相之所代理
者也分之當然也而非以為功也身視天下
者則以君為元首臣為股肱言元首之尊實
===
股肱之所捍衛者也勢之必然也而非以為
恩也是道也即大學之道也即止仁止敬之
說也臣嘗莊誦曾子之訓而至於篇終因重
有感矣彼治平之要莫大於絜矩絜矩之義
莫先於公好惡而其所謂公好惡者則首曰
用人如惟仁人能好人能惡人是也次曰理
財如生財有大道是也人者國之楨榦使國
無其人則誰與共理是猶操舟而舍柁師矣
財者國之命脉使財用不足則國空虛是猶
治家而忘稼穡矣故有其人無其財則國家

…is Heaven’s intent. Yet the means by which it nurtures and cherishes living things are simply the sun to warm them, rain to moisten them, wind to breathe upon them, and thunder to stir them; Heaven does not itself perform these tasks. Compare this to the management of a great household’s estate: from the major labors of plowing, harvesting, weaving, and spinning to the minor duties of sweeping, cleaning, answering calls, and receiving guests, its descendants and servants divide the responsibilities and perform them on its behalf. The stern father need only oversee the guiding principles and receive reports of what has been accomplished. How, then, is the relationship between ruler and ministers any different? Thus, when All under Heaven is viewed as a family, the ruler is its lineage head and the ministers its household stewards. This means that the lineage head’s affairs are all managed on his behalf by the household stewards: this is what their allotted duties require, and they do not count it as a meritorious achievement. When All under Heaven is viewed as a body, the ruler is its head and the ministers its limbs. This means that the exalted head is protected by the limbs: this necessarily follows from their relationship, and they do not count it as a favor bestowed. This way is precisely the way of the Great Learning—the teaching that the ruler should abide in benevolence and the minister in reverence.

Your servant once solemnly recited Master Zeng’s teachings, and on reaching the end of the text was moved to further reflection. Among the essentials of governing the state and bringing peace to All under Heaven, none is greater than applying the measuring square of reciprocity; in the meaning of that principle, nothing takes precedence over impartiality in likes and dislikes. What is meant by such impartiality concerns, first, employing men, as in the statement, “Only a benevolent person can love others and hate others”; and second, managing wealth, as in the statement, “There is a great way to produce wealth.” Men are the pillars of the state. …the state's primal vitality is insufficient; if it has wealth but lacks capable men, its animating spirit cannot flourish. These two things are indeed indispensable to government: neither can be neglected. Yet, when we examine their particulars, must all necessarily be undertaken by the ruler himself? The ruler is the mind and will; his ministers are the body's many parts. Whatever the mind wishes to do, the body's parts must obey its commands; whatever the ruler wishes to do, the various offices must respectfully carry out. Thus, setting his purpose on employing capable men is the ruler's duty, but it is the Minister of Personnel and the Minister of Rites who actually hold the balance in promoting the worthy, selecting impartially, choosing talent, and assigning responsibilities. Setting his purpose on managing wealth is the ruler's duty, but it is the Minister of Revenue and the Minister of Works who actually perform the tasks of assessing tribute according to the land's resources, assembling artisans, and gathering wealth.
Let us test this against antiquity. In discerning men's abilities and bringing peace to the people, Yao and Shun certainly employed capable men, yet they did not personally undertake everything. Clearly recommending men from humble and obscure stations, receiving their counsel together, and putting it broadly into practice were matters they entrusted to the regional chiefs and governors. In assessing levies according to the soil, Yao and Shun certainly managed wealth, yet they did not personally undertake everything. Providing the people with grain earned through toil and vigorously exchanging surpluses for what was lacking were matters they entrusted to Yu and Yi. Thereafter, the Three Dynasties arose in succession and followed this method. I have examined the Royal Regulations and the Rites of Zhou: those advanced to the Minister of Education were called ‘selected scholars’; those advanced to the Minister of War were called ‘advanced scholars’ (jinshi). Only after further assessment and discrimination were they assigned duties; only thereafter were they granted rank, and only once their positions were settled were they given stipends. Thus, the Three Dynasties were thorough and cautious in employing men. Yet when the texts speak of the Minister of Education and the Minister of War, what part of this was not performed by their various officials? There was a Controller of Receipts to audit incoming wealth and goods, and a Controller of Expenditures to audit outgoing wealth and goods. text:
歲會考歲成是三代之理財者周且密矣而
曰職內曰職歲亦何莫非其百執事之所為
也夫語事之大者莫過於用人理財語治之
極者莫過於唐虞三代而皆其公卿百執事
有以代為之則上古君逸臣勞與夫一德一
心之義不章章乎有明徵也哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝紹統帝王鑒觀成憲尤惓惓於大學
衍義之書而一時名世之臣又皆景附雲從
效忠宣力於其下於凡明德新民之事齊家
治國平天下之法靡不纖悉具舉以言乎用
===
人也則賓興既徧于有司而公察舉嚴考課
凡所以鼓舞而督責者又未嘗無勸懲之術
以言乎理財也則額辦既取諸二稅而廣屯
田清鹽法凡所以兼資而並濟者又未嘗無
通變之權故當是時庶務叢委而銓曹無乏
人之患征伐四出而司農無告匱之憂良有
以也肆我
皇上壽考作人恭儉為國而正文體端士風蠲民
租汰冗費且屢厪
明詔焉則夫菁莪樂育之下家稷契而戶詩書府

…and used the annual accounts to assess the year’s accomplishments. Thus the financial administration of the Three Dynasties was comprehensive and meticulous. Yet those called the officials in charge of receipts and annual expenditures—were they not likewise among the many officials who carried out these tasks? Among the great affairs of government, none surpass employing men and managing finances; among the highest achievements of government, none surpass those of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Their dukes, ministers, and many officials all performed these tasks on their rulers’ behalf. Is this not manifest evidence of the ancient principle that the ruler rests while his ministers labor, and that they share one virtue and one mind?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao continued the succession of the ancient emperors and kings, examined their established institutions, and devoted particular attention to the book Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi). The eminent ministers of his age all followed him like shadows and gathering clouds, rendering loyal service and exerting their strength under him. In everything concerning the illumination of virtue and the renewal of the people, and in the methods of ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to All-under-Heaven, nothing was left unimplemented, down to the smallest detail. As for employing men, the practice of honoring and recommending worthy candidates was already widespread among the responsible authorities; recommendations were made impartially and evaluations conducted rigorously. In all the means used to encourage men and hold them accountable, methods of reward and punishment were never lacking. As for managing finances, the prescribed revenue was obtained through the two seasonal taxes, while agricultural colonies were expanded and the salt administration set in order. In all the means used to draw upon complementary resources and meet needs together, discretion to adapt to changing circumstances was never lacking. Thus, at that time, although manifold affairs crowded in, the Ministry of Personnel had no concern about a shortage of men; although military expeditions went out in every direction, the minister responsible for revenue had no fear of reporting empty coffers. There was good reason for this.
Now our August Sovereign, blessed with longevity, nurtures men of talent and governs the realm with reverence and frugality. He corrects literary style, rectifies the conduct of scholars, remits the people’s land taxes, and eliminates unnecessary expenditure; he has repeatedly taken the trouble to issue enlightened edicts on these matters. …with the treasuries filled to overflowing, grain grows old and rots, and the strings on which cash is threaded decay. The people have indeed enjoyed days of joyful peace. Yet in recent years, although many possess the integrity celebrated in the lines about lambskin robes and plain silk, it cannot be said that there are none of those men whose conduct fails to befit their robes. Although the abundance celebrated in “our stacks of grain number in the hundreds of millions” remains as it was before, it cannot be said that there are none who, in the lesser and greater eastern regions, have empty looms. Alas! Why is this so? It is because longstanding laws breed abuses, and profound imperial favor allows men’s resolve to grow lax. Although the sagely Son of Heaven above them daily bears cares that keep him awake at night and delay his meals, the responsible officials cannot fully comprehend and embody his intentions. Their execution of his benevolent purposes remains incomplete.
Looking at matters today, edicts enjoining compassion in punishments have been issued, yet wolves are set to shepherd sheep, and the realm daily sinks further into brutality. Edicts inculcating incorruptibility have been issued, yet men bring destruction upon themselves through their greed, like creatures destroyed for their tusks, and the realm daily deteriorates through corruption. Schools are the gateway for worthy scholars, but if lectures and explanations merely meet the demands of elaborate formalities, what means are there to cultivate a reserve of talent? Surveillance commissioners distinguish the loyal from the wicked, but if praise and blame arise chiefly from personal likes and dislikes, on what basis can recommendations and impeachments be made? Although Your Majesty is deeply concerned with policies for employing men, this is how the responsible officials implement them. Is there not, then, a reason why men of talent have not all become worthy?
Edicts encouraging agriculture have been issued, yet men idle about in the morning and sing in the evening, and the realm suffers increasingly from indolence. Edicts honoring frugality have been issued, yet men adorn themselves with strings of pearls and assorted silk braids, and the realm daily pursues greater extravagance. Annual levies are certainly proper to collect, but if one levy is used as a pretext for another, what justification is there? Supplies for the imperial court are certainly …

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
所當用而以一科十則何謂也
陛下雖切切於理財之策而其奉行於有司者乃
如是焉則財用之未能盡充也不有由然乎
人各務厭其欲而曾不以
陛下之心為心人各自私其利而曾不以天下之
利為利欺
君欺
天害民害物誠有如
聖制所云者矣嗚呼知弊之所由生則知所以革
弊之故知法之所由弛則知所以更法之原
===
然則將如之何亦惟即其不能不敝之法消
息損益之而已爾是故申察舉之公則十科
取士司馬光之疏於宋者可采而行也嚴考
課之法則中正九品陳群之創於魏者可采
而行也或為寇準之却例簿而使停解日月
者無坐遷之望或為漢宣之覈名實而使偽
增戶口者無濫竽之賞至如周禮以八柄馭
群臣以八法治官府則尤其所當亟講者焉
復屯田之額則軍民錯處趙充國之困先零
者可采而行也清鹽鹺之弊則載米易鹽李

然則將如之何？亦惟即其不能不敝之法，消息損益之而已爾。是故申察舉之公，則十科取士，司馬光之疏於宋者，可采而行也；嚴考課之法，則中正九品，陳群之創於魏者，可采而行也。或為寇準之却例簿，而使停解日月者無坐遷之望；或為漢宣之覈名實，而使偽增戶口者無濫竽之賞。至如《周禮》以八柄馭群臣，以八法治官府，則尤其所當亟講者焉。復屯田之額，則軍民錯處，趙充國之困先零者，可采而行也；清鹽鹺之弊，則載米易鹽，李
translation_en:
…are indeed proper expenditures; but what does it mean to levy ten for every one required? Although Your Majesty is deeply concerned with policies for managing finances, this is how the responsible officials implement them. Is there not, then, a reason why financial resources remain insufficient? Everyone strives to satisfy his own desires, never taking Your Majesty’s concerns as his own; everyone pursues his private advantage, never treating the interests of all under Heaven as his own. They deceive their sovereign and Heaven, harm the people and injure all things: truly, matters are as Your Majesty’s decree describes. Alas! Understanding how abuses arise reveals the means of reforming them; understanding how laws become lax reveals the basis for revising them.

What, then, should be done? Simply take those laws that inevitably deteriorate and adjust them, making reductions and additions as circumstances require. Thus, to reaffirm impartiality in selection through investigation and recommendation, we may adopt the selection of men under ten categories that Sima Guang proposed in a memorial during the Song. To make performance evaluations rigorous, we may adopt the nine-rank system of Rectifiers that Chen Qun established in the Wei. We might follow Kou Zhun in rejecting the register of precedents, so that those relying on the time elapsed since suspension or discharge [?] have no hope of gaining promotion merely by waiting. Or we might follow Emperor Xuan of the Han in checking actual performance against reported claims, so that those who falsely inflate household and population figures receive no rewards to which they are not entitled. As for the Rites of Zhou, which uses eight prerogatives to govern the assembled ministers and eight regulations to administer government offices, these especially deserve urgent study. To restore the prescribed scale of agricultural colonies, we may adopt Zhao Chongguo’s practice of settling soldiers and civilians together, by which he wore down the Xianling. To eliminate abuses in the salt administration, we may adopt the transport of rice to exchange for salt, as Li…

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
沆之遣發運者可采而行也或汰不急之員
則蘇軾之三冗可除而凡冒濫者皆在所必
去或撤無名之費則李泌之三盈可節而凡
卮漏者皆在所必省至如周禮以九賦斂財
賄以九式均財用則尤其所當亟講者焉然
此數事者
陛下非必自為而可也銓衡之務則以責成冢宰
選舉之務則以責成宗伯錢穀之務則以責
成司徒營作之務則以責成司空在外則以
責成撫按藩臬而
===
陛下乃時省厥成如其底可績也則曰惟爾之能
如其奏罔功也則曰惟爾不任譬猶於穆之
命默運於重玄之表而四時之官五行之吏
因以分職而迭任焉在
廷諸臣其誰敢不竭思而盡忠乎然則天不勞
而化功著亦握其樞焉已爾君不勞而治功
成亦舉其綱焉已爾由是用人不必
陛下之自為也而諸臣皆有以代為之為山濤之
甄別人物為房琯之推轂士類為趙武之舉
管庫七十有餘家而所謂知無不舉舉無不

陛下之自爲也而諸臣皆有以代爲之爲山濤之
甄別人物爲房琯之推轂士類爲趙武之舉
管庫七十有餘家而所謂知無不舉舉無不
punctuated:
沆之遣發運者，可采而行也。或汰不急之員，則蘇軾之三冗可除，而凡冒濫者皆在所必去；或撤無名之費，則李泌之三盈可節，而凡卮漏者皆在所必省。至如《周禮》以九賦斂財賄，以九式均財用，則尤其所當亟講者焉。
然此數事者，陛下非必自為而可也。銓衡之務，則以責成冢宰；選舉之務，則以責成宗伯；錢穀之務，則以責成司徒；營作之務，則以責成司空。在外，則以責成撫按藩臬，而陛下乃時省厥成。如其底可績也，則曰：「惟爾之能。」如其奏罔功也，則曰：「惟爾不任。」譬猶於穆之命，默運於重玄之表，而四時之官、五行之吏，因以分職而迭任焉。在廷諸臣，其誰敢不竭思而盡忠乎？然則天不勞而化功著，亦握其樞焉已爾；君不勞而治功成，亦舉其綱焉已爾。
由是用人不必陛下之自為也，而諸臣皆有以代為之：為山濤之甄別人物，為房琯之推轂士類，為趙武之舉管庫七十有餘家，而所謂知無不舉，舉無不
translation_en:
…Li Hang’s dispatch of Transport Commissioners is a practice that may be adopted and implemented. If unnecessary posts are eliminated, the three forms of redundancy identified by Su Shi can be removed, and all who have obtained office fraudulently or improperly must be dismissed. If unwarranted expenses are abolished, Li Mi’s “three surpluses” can be curtailed [?], and every source of financial leakage must be checked. Above all, the methods in the Rites of Zhou for collecting wealth and goods through the nine levies and regulating expenditure through the nine standards urgently deserve examination.
Yet Your Majesty need not personally undertake these several tasks. Responsibility for personnel appointments should be entrusted to the Minister of Personnel; for selecting candidates through examinations, to the Minister of Rites; for revenue in money and grain, to the Minister of Revenue; and for construction, to the Minister of Works. Outside the capital, responsibility should be entrusted to Grand Coordinators, Regional Inspectors, Provincial Administration Commissioners, and Provincial Surveillance Commissioners. Your Majesty need only inspect their accomplishments from time to time. If they achieve results worthy of recognition, say: “This is your ability.” If their efforts yield no results, say: “You are unequal to your charge.” This resembles the profound and august mandate of Heaven, operating silently beyond the highest heavens, while the officers of the four seasons and the functionaries of the five phases divide their duties and take their turns in service. Which of the ministers at court would then dare fail to exert his utmost thought and devotion? Thus Heaven achieves manifest transformations without toil, simply by holding their pivot; the ruler achieves good government without toil, simply by grasping its guiding cord.
Accordingly, Your Majesty need not personally attend to employing men, for the ministers can all act on your behalf: distinguishing and appraising men as Shan Tao did, recommending worthy scholars as Fang Guan did, and promoting men from more than seventy households of storehouse keepers as Zhao Wu did. This is what is meant by “leaving none whom one knows unrecommended, and none whom one recommends…”

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
先者在是也由是理財亦不必
陛下之自為也而諸臣皆有以代為之為陸贄之
酌盈濟虛為曾鞏之去浮從約為劉晏之歲
增鹽利六百餘萬緡而所謂為之者疾用之
者舒者在是也
聖制謂用得其人政自治財理得宜用自足斯言
也其真萬世之格言矣乎雖然理財急矣用
人尤為要也大學治平之訓雖以二者並言
而篇終覆論理財則尤以小人為戒盖政事
之失由官邪也官之失職寵賂章也故未有
===
用得其人而財不裕者亦未有用之匪人而
財可裕者今
陛下嘉惠元元殆靡所弗至而官民兩竭率患於
財用之未敷者亦或職此之故耳然則
聖制之所詢者雖兼以用人理財為重而臣之所
望於
今日以為當加意焉者則尤拳拳於用人之圖也
抑臣復有獻焉昔大學論好惡公私之極而
必總結之曰君子有大道必忠信以得之是
知用人者理財之要也純心者用人之本也

必總結之曰君子有大道必忠信以得之是
知用人者理財之要也純心者用人之本也
punctuated:
先者，在是也。由是理財亦不必陛下之自為也，而諸臣皆有以代為之：為陸贄之酌盈濟虛，為曾鞏之去浮從約，為劉晏之歲增鹽利六百餘萬緡，而所謂為之者疾、用之者舒者，在是也。
聖制謂：「用得其人，政自治；財理得宜，用自足。」斯言也，其真萬世之格言矣乎！雖然，理財急矣，用人尤為要也。《大學》治平之訓，雖以二者並言，而篇終覆論理財，則尤以小人為戒。盖政事之失，由官邪也；官之失職，寵賂章也。故未有用得其人而財不裕者，亦未有用之匪人而財可裕者。今陛下嘉惠元元，殆靡所弗至，而官民兩竭，率患於財用之未敷者，亦或職此之故耳。然則聖制之所詢者，雖兼以用人理財為重，而臣之所望於今日，以為當加意焉者，則尤拳拳於用人之圖也。
抑臣復有獻焉。昔《大學》論好惡公私之極，而必總結之曰：「君子有大道，必忠信以得之。」是知用人者，理財之要也；純心者，用人之本也。
translation_en:
…giving precedence to those recommended: this is what that means. Likewise, Your Majesty need not personally manage the finances, for all your ministers can act on your behalf: emulating Lu Zhi in drawing upon surpluses to remedy shortages, Zeng Gong in eliminating extravagance and practicing economy, and Liu Yan in increasing annual salt revenues by more than six million strings of cash. This is what is meant by producing wealth swiftly and spending it slowly.
Your Majesty’s decree states: “If the right people are employed, government will naturally be well ordered; if finances are properly managed, resources will naturally suffice.” Truly, are these not guiding words for all ages? Nevertheless, urgent though financial management is, employing the right people is still more essential. Although the Great Learning discusses both together in its teachings on ordering the state and bringing peace to the realm, when it returns to financial management at the end, it particularly warns against petty men. Failures in government arise from corrupt officials; officials’ neglect of their duties arises from the prevalence of favoritism and bribery. Thus there has never been a case in which the right people were employed yet the finances failed to prosper, nor one in which unworthy people were employed yet the finances could prosper. Now Your Majesty extends gracious care to the common people in almost every conceivable way, yet both the authorities and the people are depleted, continually troubled by insufficient resources. This, too, may be attributable to that cause. Thus, although Your Majesty’s decree asks about both personnel appointments and financial management as matters of importance, what your servant hopes will receive particular attention today is, above all, the planning of appointments.
Your servant has a further observation to offer. The Great Learning, after discussing to the utmost whether likes and dislikes serve the public good or private interests, concludes with these words: “The gentleman has a great Way; he must attain it through loyalty and trustworthiness.” From this we know that employing the right people is the key to managing finances, and purity of heart is the foundation of employing the right people.

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
誠正者又事心之功也我
皇上敬一之箴出自
淵衷其曰
郊則恭誠
廟嚴孝趨肅于明廷慎于閒居非所謂誠意乎其
曰勿參以三勿貳以二行顧其言終如其始
非所謂正心乎然則君子平天下之大道固

陛下之一心而裕如矣而臣猶贅贅於此者非欲
於敬一之外有所加也惟欲由此心而涵泳
===

荒者帝王之心臣願
陛下益澄神於宥密之中常勅天於時幾之際使
此心之敬者無時而不用其敬此心之一者
無時而不用其一如日月之久照而不毁其
明焉如四時之久行而不窮其紀焉如天地
之久運而不息其機焉則德以緝熈而愈盛
道以涵養而愈純用人理財之要固體會於
身心而久安長治之猷益光昭於華夏矣臣
不識忌諱干冒

translation_en:
…Making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind are, in turn, the work of cultivating the mind. Our Emperor’s Admonition on Reverent Oneness (Jingyi zhen) issues from the depths of his heart. It says: “At the suburban sacrifices, be reverent and sincere; in the ancestral temple, solemnly hasten in filial devotion [?]; be solemn in the public court and circumspect in private.” Is this not what is meant by making the intentions sincere? It says: “Do not introduce a third and make it three; do not introduce a second and make it two. Let your conduct accord with your words, and end as you began.” Is this not what is meant by rectifying the mind? Thus, the great Way by which the gentleman brings peace to all under Heaven is already abundantly available within Your Majesty’s single mind. If your servant nevertheless dwells repetitively upon this, it is not because I wish to add anything beyond reverent oneness, but only because I wish you, through this mind, to immerse yourself in it without end.

Daily renewal, followed by further renewal, is the learning of the sage; freedom from indolence and neglect is the mind of the true sovereign. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would further clarify your spirit in profound stillness and constantly heed Heaven [?] at the critical beginnings of events. Let the reverence of this mind always be put into practice, and let its oneness always be put into practice. Be like the sun and moon, which shine enduringly without impairing their brightness; like the four seasons, which proceed enduringly without exhausting their ordered sequence; and like Heaven and Earth, which revolve enduringly without their workings ever ceasing. Then your virtue, through continuing illumination, will become ever more abundant, and your Way, through nurturing, ever purer. The essentials of employing men and managing wealth will indeed be embodied and understood in your person and mind, while your plans for lasting peace and enduring good government will shine ever more brightly throughout Huaxia. Your servant, ignorant of what is forbidden to say, presumes to offend …

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
臣林士章
臣對臣聞代天出治者人君之責為君者常
以天之心為心輔君致治者人臣之責為臣
者當以君之心為心以天為心者必求盡所
以代天之道是謂盛世之君以君為心者必
求盡所以輔君之職是謂盛世之臣二者相
期相濟以措天下於永寧之域而使斯世斯
民無匹夫匹婦之不得其所者也然心天之
心者敬而已矣心君之心者亦敬而已矣敬
也者固修己以安百姓之要道也為大君者
===
既不遑寧處而欲法天以下濟乎群生則為
臣者當恪共匪懈而一乃心以上媚于天子
苟心有弗敬敬有弗純是自欺也自欺者始
雖欺己而至於欺天欺君蠹國害民皆自是
致之矣有臣若此是豈君之心亦豈天之心
也耶臣竊伏草茅求諸古訓至天佑下民作
之君師仰而言曰天下之民至衆也而一人
之身實寄之為君者如何而不以天為心也
至孔子告哀公臣事君以忠則又作而嘆曰
人君一身責甚繁也而輔弼之臣實代之為

translation_en:
Your servant, Lin Shizhang.

Your servant replies: I have heard that to govern on Heaven’s behalf is the ruler’s responsibility; a ruler must always take Heaven’s heart as his own. To assist the ruler in achieving good government is the minister’s responsibility; a minister ought to take the ruler’s heart as his own. One who takes Heaven’s heart as his own must seek to fulfill completely the Way of acting on Heaven’s behalf: such is the ruler of a flourishing age. One who takes the ruler’s heart as his own must seek to discharge fully the duties of assisting his ruler: such is the minister of a flourishing age. These two hold one another to these expectations and support one another, bringing all under Heaven into lasting peace, so that among the people of their age not a single man or woman fails to find a proper place. Yet to make Heaven’s heart one’s own requires nothing other than reverent attentiveness; to make the ruler’s heart one’s own likewise requires nothing other than reverent attentiveness. Reverent attentiveness is indeed the essential Way of cultivating oneself so as to bring peace to the common people. Since the sovereign allows himself no leisure to rest and wishes to emulate Heaven in extending aid to all living beings below, his ministers ought to be respectfully diligent and unremitting, making their hearts single in purpose so as to please the Son of Heaven above. If the heart lacks reverence, or its reverence lacks purity, this is self-deception. Though those who deceive themselves begin by deceiving only themselves, their eventual deception of Heaven and the ruler, their corruption of the state and harm to the people, all arise from this. If there are ministers like this, how could their hearts be those of the ruler, or indeed those of Heaven?

Your servant, dwelling obscurely among the common people, has sought understanding in ancient teachings. On reaching the words, “Heaven aids the people below, establishing rulers and teachers for them,” I looked up and said: “The people of all under Heaven are exceedingly numerous, yet responsibility for them is entrusted to a single person. How can a ruler fail to take Heaven’s heart as his own?” On reaching Confucius’s words to Duke Ai, “A minister serves his ruler with loyalty,” I then rose and sighed: “The ruler is but one person, and his responsibilities are exceedingly numerous; his assisting ministers act on his behalf. title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
臣者苟不體君之心將何以代其終而慰吾
君也是故君盡君道臣盡臣道明良協德交
警不怠臣於
今日端有望焉茲與有司之選仰承
大廷之對敢不自竭愚誠以對颺
休命於萬一乎恭惟
皇帝陛下大道冲和至誠悠久體三才而弘化秉

translation_en:
…those serving as ministers, if they do not make their ruler’s heart their own, how can they bring his work to completion on his behalf and comfort their sovereign? Thus the ruler must fulfill the Way of the ruler, and ministers the Way of ministers. An enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers must unite in virtue and tirelessly admonish one another. This is precisely what your servant hopes for today. Having now been selected by the responsible officials and honored with the opportunity to answer at the great court, dare I fail to exhaust my humble sincerity, so as to respond to and extol even a ten-thousandth part of your gracious command?

I reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor embodies the harmonious balance of the great Way and an utmost sincerity that endures without cease. You embody the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—to extend your transforming influence, and maintain single-minded reverence to establish the Mean. Since ascending the throne, you have invariably appointed suitable men, so that men like Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie stand among your officials. Your conduct of government has invariably been fitting, so that rites, music, administration, and punishments have spread far and wide. Men of virtue cleanse their hearts to receive your gracious virtue, while the common people, steeped in its influence, rejoice in great peace. The broad reach of your sagely transformation is indeed so vast that it defies description. Yet, sage though you are, you do not regard yourself as a sage, and always feel keenly that you have not attained your goal. Though the realm is well governed, you act as if it were not yet so, constantly cherishing the people as though they were wounded.

At the beginning of the imperial policy question, you say: “I reverently receive High Heaven’s luminous mandate and rule these Chinese and non-Chinese peoples. Day and night I maintain reverence, daring neither to be negligent nor to indulge myself. My one concern is for the people: I wish everyone to find a proper place.” Your servant has reverently read and pondered these words, and thereby understands that Your Majesty’s entire achievement in preserving good government can be accomplished through this single concern. This heart is the very heart with which High Heaven brings living things into being; this Way is the very Way by which the Sovereign Ultimate is widely bestowed. Only…

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
天聰明惟聖時憲言君道之至者孰有加於
此乎臣觀自古稱盛治者莫過於唐虞語至
德者莫過於堯舜然堯之為君欽若昊天其
心也至究其德之大則曰其仁如天夫惟有
敬天之心是以有合天之道舜之為君敕天
之命其心也至究其功之隆則曰好生之德
洽于民心夫惟有純天之德是以有體天之
化傳曰天地之大德曰生堯舜蓋善體之矣
又曰天視自我民視天聽自我民聽堯舜蓋
奉若之矣故考其時百姓昭明萬邦協和四
===
方風動鳳凰來儀不惟下民之祗協而蠻貊
罔不率俾暨山川鳥獸亦罔不咸若治功之
成巍然煥然夫豈無所自哉
陛下撫堯舜中天之運存堯舜愛民之心治化所
彰宜其駕唐虞而上之矣而一念之敬畏常
歉然不敢自寧者臣愚以為是體
天之心者也堯舜在上萬民樂生熈熈皞皞固宜
在在而皆然矣然猶以安百姓為已病而下
民其咨黎民阻飢之慮尚未釋然也
陛下安能忘是心哉然臣甞聞之統天下之治存乎

成巍巍然煥煥然夫豈無所自哉
陛下撫堯舜中天之運存堯舜愛民之心治化所
彰宜其駕唐虞而上之矣而一念之敬畏常
懔然不敢自寧者臣愚以為是體

在在而皆然矣然猶以安百姓為已病而下
民其咨黎民阻饑之慮尚未釋然也
陛下安能忘是心哉然臣嘗聞之統天下之治存
punctuated:
天聰明，惟聖時憲。言君道之至者，孰有加於此乎？臣觀自古稱盛治者，莫過於唐虞；語至德者，莫過於堯舜。然堯之為君，欽若昊天，其心也至；究其德之大，則曰：「其仁如天。」夫惟有敬天之心，是以有合天之道。舜之為君，敕天之命，其心也至；究其功之隆，則曰：「好生之德，洽于民心。」夫惟有純天之德，是以有體天之化。傳曰：「天地之大德曰生。」堯舜蓋善體之矣。又曰：「天視自我民視，天聽自我民聽。」堯舜蓋奉若之矣。故考其時，百姓昭明，萬邦協和，四方風動，鳳凰來儀。不惟下民之祗協，而蠻貊罔不率俾，暨山川鳥獸，亦罔不咸若。治功之成，巍然煥然，夫豈無所自哉？
陛下撫堯舜中天之運，存堯舜愛民之心，治化所彰，宜其駕唐虞而上之矣。而一念之敬畏，常歉然不敢自寧者，臣愚以為是體天之心者也。堯舜在上，萬民樂生，熈熈皞皞，固宜在在而皆然矣。然猶以安百姓為已病，而下民其咨、黎民阻飢之慮，尚未釋然也。陛下安能忘是心哉？然臣甞聞之，統天下之治存乎
translation_en:
…Heaven is clear-sighted and keen of hearing; the sage takes it as his model. What statement of the highest way of rulership could surpass this? Your servant observes that, from antiquity, no flourishing government has been more highly praised than that of Tang and Yu, and no consummate virtue more highly esteemed than that of Yao and Shun. As ruler, Yao reverently conformed to august Heaven: his heart was utterly sincere. Yet when the greatness of his virtue is examined, it is said, “His benevolence was like Heaven.” Precisely because he had a heart that revered Heaven, his way accorded with Heaven. As ruler, Shun attended reverently to Heaven’s mandate: his heart was utterly sincere. Yet when the grandeur of his achievements is examined, it is said, “His virtue of cherishing life permeated the people’s hearts.” Precisely because his virtue was wholly of Heaven, his transforming influence embodied Heaven’s workings. The Commentary says, “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is to give life.” Yao and Shun surely embodied this well. It also says, “Heaven sees through what our people see; Heaven hears through what our people hear.” Yao and Shun surely obeyed and followed this. Thus, examining their age, we find the people enlightened, the myriad states harmonized, the four quarters stirred as by the wind, and phoenixes arriving in stately array. Not only were the common people reverently united, but the Man and Mo peoples all obeyed; even the mountains and rivers, birds and beasts, were all in due accord. Their achievements in government were lofty and resplendent. Could these have been without a source?
Your Majesty presides over an age of ascendancy like that of Yao and Shun and cherishes their love for the people. The manifest effects of your government and transforming influence ought therefore to surpass those of Tang and Yu. Yet your reverence and awe leave you ever conscious of inadequacy, never daring to rest content. Your foolish servant considers this the heart that embodies Heaven. With Yao and Shun above, the myriad people delighted in life, joyful and at ease; surely this should have been so everywhere. Yet they still regarded bringing peace to the people as a task that taxed their powers [?], and their concern over the common people’s lamentations and the populace’s suffering from hunger had still not been dispelled. How could Your Majesty forget this heart? Yet your servant has heard that the unification of government throughout All-under-Heaven rests with…

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
乎君輔天下之治存乎臣堯舜存心於天下
加志於窮民固至矣而左右賛襄之臣所以
協恭而和衷者若羲和之勤其官而歳序以
定四岳之修其職而九牧以倡益掌山澤而
物害以除臯陶為士而五教以弼伯夷典禮
后夔典樂而中和之化備稷播百榖禹治洪
水而安養之道周凡所以備翼為明聽之任
而代天以出治者固各有其人矣凡所以效
翼為明聽之能而輔君以成化者又各盡其
心矣今
===
陛下軫念民瘼常若恐恐逺邇之臣凡有血氣者
固宜奉承不懈使德澤下究斯民蒙乎至治
也然而未明乎靖共之節者惟因循之是便
未盡乎旬宣之義者惟私橐之是謀致
陛下宵旰之懷懇懇及此夫有
君如是而忍負之必無人心者也臣聞堯舜之憂
民可謂至矣一時效忠之臣亦無不盡矣然
而猶有靜言庸違之鯀比周為黨之共工蓋
治世不能無小人而難乎其為小人堯舜不
以伯鯀共工而廢至治後世亦不因伯鯀共

乎君，輔天下之治存乎臣。堯舜存心於天下，加志於窮民，固至矣。而左右賛襄之臣，所以協恭而和衷者，若羲和之勤其官而歳序以定，四岳之修其職而九牧以倡，益掌山澤而物害以除，臯陶為士而五教以弼，伯夷典禮，后夔典樂，而中和之化備；稷播百榖，禹治洪水，而安養之道周。凡所以備翼為明聽之任，而代天以出治者，固各有其人矣；凡所以效翼為明聽之能，而輔君以成化者，又各盡其心矣。
今陛下軫念民瘼，常若恐恐，逺邇之臣，凡有血氣者，固宜奉承不懈，使德澤下究，斯民蒙乎至治也。然而未明乎靖共之節者，惟因循之是便；未盡乎旬宣之義者，惟私橐之是謀。致陛下宵旰之懷，懇懇及此。夫有君如是而忍負之，必無人心者也。臣聞堯舜之憂民，可謂至矣，一時效忠之臣，亦無不盡矣。然而猶有靜言庸違之鯀，比周為黨之共工。蓋治世不能無小人，而難乎其為小人。堯舜不以伯鯀共工而廢至治，後世亦不因伯鯀共
translation_en:
…rests with the ruler; assisting in the governance of All-under-Heaven rests with his ministers. Yao and Shun devoted their hearts to All-under-Heaven and directed their attention to the destitute: their concern was indeed consummate. As for the ministers who assisted them on either side, they worked together reverently and with one accord. Xi and He diligently discharged their offices, thereby establishing the sequence of the seasons. The Four Mountains fulfilled their duties, thereby providing leadership for the Nine Regional Governors. Yi administered the mountains and marshes, eliminating harmful creatures. Gao Yao served as Director of Justice, thereby supporting the Five Teachings. Bo Yi directed ritual, and Hou Kui directed music, bringing to completion the transforming influence of equilibrium and harmony. Ji sowed the various grains, and Yu controlled the floods, making complete the means of securing and nourishing the people. For every responsibility of assisting the ruler as his wings and helping him to see clearly and hear distinctly, and thus of administering government on Heaven’s behalf, there were indeed the appropriate men. In exercising these capacities and assisting the ruler in accomplishing moral transformation, each also devoted himself wholeheartedly.
Now Your Majesty is deeply concerned about the people’s suffering, constantly seeming apprehensive. All ministers, near and far—indeed, all who possess flesh and blood—ought surely to carry out your intentions without flagging, so that your beneficence reaches those below and the people enjoy consummate government. Yet those who do not understand the obligations of respectful service seek only the convenience of following established routines; those who do not fully discharge their duty to spread your beneficence seek only to fill their own purses. Thus Your Majesty’s concern, which keeps you occupied before dawn and until late in the day, has become as earnest as this. Anyone who has such a ruler and can bear to betray him must surely lack a human heart. Your servant has heard that Yao and Shun’s concern for the people may be called consummate, and that the ministers who served them loyally in their time likewise spared no effort. Yet there were still Gun, whose fine words concealed disobedient conduct, and Gong Gong, who colluded with others to form a faction. Even a well-governed age cannot be without petty men, but it makes it difficult for them to act as petty men. Yao and Shun did not allow the Earl of Gun and Gong Gong to thwart their consummate government; nor did later generations, on account of the Earl of Gun and Gong…

工而議堯舜之治也今
陛下如有此輩則屏之遠方終身不齒可也甚者
置之憲典可也凡為臣者孰不洗心滌慮竦
懼而思警乎
聖制有曰大學之道專以用人理財為急用得其
人政自治財理得宜用自足
陛下之言及此誠致治之要樞也臣請以大學之
意言之夫大學釋治平之旨莫先於絜矩之
道絜矩者平天下之大端公天下之大本也
人君一心運之於淵嘿之地而實放之於四
===
海之廣發之於一念之微而實公之於兆民
之眾
陛下念及於民欲人人得其所此固絜矩之心也

天命者也用失其人則惟掊克是事惟聚斂
是謀始也剥民以病國終至民困而國貧所
謂失眾失國而失天命者也故財之理必先

…Gong Gong as grounds for criticizing the government of Yao and Shun. Now, if Your Majesty has men of this sort, you may banish them to distant regions and exclude them from office for life; in graver cases, you may subject them to the penalties prescribed by law. What servant of the throne would then fail to cleanse his heart and purify his thoughts, trembling in fear and taking warning?
Your sacred decree says: “The Way of the Great Learning gives particular urgency to employing men and managing wealth. Employ the right men, and government will naturally be well ordered; manage wealth appropriately, and resources will naturally suffice.” Your Majesty’s words on this matter truly address the essential pivot of good government. Your servant asks leave to explain this through the meaning of the Great Learning. In explaining the principles of governing the state and bringing peace to the world, the Great Learning places nothing before the Way of ‘measuring by the square’—judging how to treat others by what one would wish for oneself. This is the chief principle for bringing peace to the world and the great foundation for impartiality throughout it. The ruler exercises his single heart in profound stillness, yet its influence truly extends across the vastness of the Four Seas; it issues from the subtle beginnings of a single thought, yet is truly shared impartially with the multitudes of the people. Your Majesty thinks of the people and wishes everyone to find their proper place: this is indeed the heart that measures by the square. By extending this heart to employing men and managing wealth, why need you fear failing to achieve these aims?
Those employed are the means of acting on the ruler’s behalf and bringing his governance to the people; wealth is what sustains the people’s lives. When the wrong men are employed, they occupy themselves solely with oppressive exactions and scheme solely to amass wealth. They begin by stripping the people and thereby harming the state; they end by reducing the people to distress and the state to poverty. title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
於用人而用人亦所以理財也書以知人安
民並舉而言之以明二者之相須而堯舜之
所加意者不越乎此而已然欲人之用必如
大學之與民同其好惡而不畜牛羊不察鷄
豚善體人君絜矩之意者是也欲用之足必
如大學之生之衆而食之寡為之疾而用之
舒因天順地而樽節愛養者是也茲其用人
理財之大致也
聖制又曰茲欲人得用財得理以至治美刑平華
尊夷遁久安長治之計何道可臻
===
陛下之言及此天下無疆之福也臣甞觀諸易曰
何以守位曰仁何以聚人曰財盖財者民之
命也欲財者民之心也奪民之財則傷民之
命傷民之命則失民之心於是有陷不義而
罹刑憲刑因之以不平者矣於是有作不典
而梗吾治治因之以不理者矣於是有逃遁
異域勾引異類以為向導而使華夷之混亂
者矣是財之聚散實係生民之休戚王道之
盛衰由此觀之久安長治之計誠莫過於理
財之得其宜而理財之宜亦惟難於理之得

盛衰由此觀之久安長治之計誠莫過於理
財之得其宜而理財之宜亦惟難於理之得
punctuated:
於用人，而用人亦所以理財也。《書》以知人安民並舉而言之，以明二者之相須，而堯舜之所加意者不越乎此而已。然欲人之用，必如《大學》之與民同其好惡，而不畜牛羊、不察鷄豚，善體人君絜矩之意者是也。欲用之足，必如《大學》之生之衆而食之寡，為之疾而用之舒，因天順地而樽節愛養者是也。茲其用人理財之大致也。
聖制又曰：「茲欲人得用、財得理，以至治美刑平、華尊夷遁，久安長治之計，何道可臻？」
陛下之言及此，天下無疆之福也。臣甞觀諸《易》曰：「何以守位？曰仁。何以聚人？曰財。」盖財者民之命也，欲財者民之心也。奪民之財，則傷民之命；傷民之命，則失民之心。於是有陷不義而罹刑憲，刑因之以不平者矣。於是有作不典而梗吾治，治因之以不理者矣。於是有逃遁異域，勾引異類以為向導，而使華夷之混亂者矣。是財之聚散，實係生民之休戚、王道之盛衰。由此觀之，久安長治之計，誠莫過於理財之得其宜，而理財之宜，亦惟難於理之得
translation_en:
…with the employment of people, and employing people is also the means of managing wealth. The Book of Documents speaks of knowing people and bringing peace to the common people together, showing their mutual dependence. What Yao and Shun devoted their attention to went no further than this. Yet those who are to be employed must be such as the Great Learning describes: sharing the people's likes and dislikes, neither keeping cattle and sheep nor scrutinizing chickens and pigs, and skillfully embodying the ruler's intent to apply the measuring square of reciprocity. To ensure sufficient resources for expenditure, one must likewise follow the Great Learning: let those who produce be many and those who consume be few; let production be swift and expenditure gradual. One must follow Heaven and accord with Earth, practicing economy and cherishing and nurturing resources. These are the broad principles of employing people and managing wealth.
The Emperor's decree further reads: “We now desire that people be properly employed and wealth properly managed, so that government may be excellent, punishments equitable, the Chinese realm honored, and the barbarians driven away. By what way can plans for enduring peace and lasting good government be realized?”
That Your Majesty's words extend to this is a boundless blessing for all under Heaven. Your servant has read in the Book of Changes: “How does one preserve one's position? Through benevolence. How does one gather people? Through wealth.” Wealth is the people's livelihood, and the desire for wealth lies in their hearts. To seize the people's wealth is to injure their livelihood; to injure their livelihood is to lose their hearts. Thus some fall into wrongdoing and incur the penalties of the law, and punishments consequently become inequitable. Others commit unlawful acts and obstruct our government, and government consequently falls into disorder. Still others flee to foreign lands, entice alien peoples to come, and serve as their guides, thereby throwing the Chinese realm and the barbarians into confusion. The concentration and dispersal of wealth thus truly determine the people's well-being or suffering and the flourishing or decline of the kingly Way. Viewed in this light, no plan for enduring peace and lasting good government can surpass the proper management of wealth. Yet the difficulty in managing wealth properly lies precisely in obtaining …

text:
其人也誠使內外之臣精白承休職理入者
倣周人九賦斂財之意職理出者倣周人九
式制用之意而官郡縣者皆能教民代田如
趙過其人焉勸民農桑如龔遂其人焉力興
水利如劉彞其人焉則凡備
聖明牧民之任者皆所以體
聖明牧民之心體
上天率育之心者也堯舜之治人既得則堯舜之
治功在此矣然而
陛下加惠元元之心有加無巳惟以人之不我用
===
而代理之責非所獨能為憂此
陛下不自用而欲用人之意也堯舜之治實資於
五臣然其始也堯以不得舜為憂舜以不得
禹臯陶為憂
陛下之意亦若是而巳矣臣聞之君者則人者也
臣者則君以自治者也故上有好者下必有
甚焉猶之盂方則水方盂圓則水圓理所必
然者陸贄有言曰漢高禀大度故時多瑰傑
不羈之才漢武好英風故時富瓌詭立名之
士漢宣精吏治故時萃循良核實之能言人

translation_en:
…the right people. If officials at court and in the provinces would truly serve with pure hearts in grateful receipt of imperial favor, those charged with managing revenue would follow the intent of the Zhou system of nine levies for collecting wealth, and those charged with managing expenditure would follow the intent of the Zhou system of nine standards for regulating its use. If those administering prefectures and counties could all teach the people the alternating-field method as Zhao Guo did, encourage farming and sericulture as Gong Sui did, and vigorously develop waterworks as Liu Yi did, then all who discharge the duty of tending the people for Your sagacious Majesty would embody Your Majesty’s concern for nurturing the people and Heaven’s concern for fostering all living things. Once men capable of governing as under Yao and Shun have been found, the achievements of Yao and Shun’s government will follow from this. Yet Your Majesty’s concern to bestow benefits upon the common people increases without cease. Your sole anxiety is that men do not serve you, while the responsibility of governing on Heaven’s behalf cannot be discharged by you alone. Yet initially Yao was anxious that he had not found Shun, and Shun was anxious that he had not found Yu and Gao Yao. Your Majesty’s intention is simply the same as theirs.

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
才惟在乎上之所率也三君固非純於王道
者然意之所向則天下随其意而趨之而况
陋三君於不屑者乎臣惟願
陛下崇寛大之體廓虚受之衷托忠賢以為腹心
開言路以廣耳目則委任責成之意既深而
媚茲
一人之心自切面從後言不必如舜之所以戒禹
凡人臣皆盡如禹之心矣啓心沃心不待如
高宗之所以望傅說凡人臣皆盡如傅說之
心矣盖手足腹心相待一體則感恩圖報者
===

盡調燮臺諫耳目之臣誠竭獻替黜陟賞罰

穀大農之臣誠慎出納郡縣綏牧之臣誠切
如保凡修諸家者皆用之於
天子之庭無有靜言庸違如鯀也無有比周為黨
如共工也濟濟多士克廣德心殆猶四時五
行各運其能以成天道保合之化山岳河海

凡人臣皆盡如禹之心矣啓心沃心不待如
高宗之所以望傅說凡人臣皆盡如傅說之
心矣蓋手足腹心相待一體則感恩圖報者
亦人之至情也況人臣又素有願忠之心者
乎由是抱先憂之志者皆懷才以效用切徇
國之心者得畢力以匡時左右輔弼之臣誠
盡調燮臺諫耳目之臣誠竭獻替黜陟賞罰
之臣誠昭國典武力將帥之臣誠固捍禦錢
穀大農之臣誠慎出納郡縣綏牧之臣誠切
如保凡修諸家者皆用之於
天子之庭無有靜言庸違如鯀也無有比周爲黨
如共工也濟濟多士克廣德心殆猶四時五
行各運其能以成天道保合之化山岳河海
punctuated:
才惟在乎上之所率也。三君固非純於王道者，然意之所向，則天下随其意而趨之，而况陋三君於不屑者乎？臣惟願陛下崇寛大之體，廓虚受之衷，托忠賢以為腹心，開言路以廣耳目，則委任責成之意既深，而媚茲一人之心自切。面從後言，不必如舜之所以戒禹，凡人臣皆盡如禹之心矣；啓心沃心，不待如高宗之所以望傅說，凡人臣皆盡如傅說之心矣。盖手足腹心相待一體，則感恩圖報者亦人之至情也，况人臣又素有願忠之心者乎？
由是抱先憂之志者，皆懷才以效用；切狥國之心者，得畢力以匡時。左右輔弼之臣，誠盡調燮；臺諫耳目之臣，誠竭獻替；黜陟賞罰之臣，誠昭國典；武力将帥之臣，誠固捍禦；錢穀大農之臣，誠慎出納；郡縣綏牧之臣，誠切如保。凡修諸家者，皆用之於天子之庭，無有靜言庸違如鯀也，無有比周為黨如共工也。濟濟多士，克廣德心，殆猶四時五行各運其能，以成天道保合之化，山岳河海
translation_en:
…talent depends entirely upon the direction given by the ruler. Those three sovereigns were certainly not wholly devoted to the Kingly Way, yet wherever their intentions inclined, all under Heaven followed. How much more would this be so under one who regards those three sovereigns as too unworthy even to emulate! Your servant wishes only that Your Majesty exalt magnanimity, enlarge your receptiveness, entrust loyal and worthy men with serving as your heart and vitals, and open the channels of counsel to extend your hearing and sight. As your commitment to delegating responsibility and holding men accountable for results deepens, their desire to please you, the One Man, will naturally become earnest. There will be no need to warn against compliance to one’s face and criticism behind one’s back, as Shun warned Yu: every minister will have a heart fully like Yu’s. There will be no need to expect ministers to enlighten and nourish the sovereign’s mind, as Gaozong expected of Fu Yue: every minister will have a heart fully like Fu Yue’s. For when limbs, heart, and vitals treat one another as parts of a single body, gratitude and the desire to repay kindness are the deepest human feelings. How much more is this true of ministers who have always wished to serve loyally!
Thus, all who aspire to be first to take on the world’s cares will bring their talents into service; those earnestly devoted to sacrificing themselves for the state will be able to exert their full strength to set the age right. Ministers who assist the sovereign at his side will sincerely do their utmost to harmonize affairs. Censors and remonstrance officials, serving as his eyes and ears, will sincerely exhaust their efforts in advancing what is good and rejecting what is wrong. Ministers responsible for demotions, promotions, rewards, and punishments will sincerely uphold the laws of the state. Military commanders will sincerely secure its defenses. Ministers responsible for revenue in money and grain will sincerely exercise care over receipts and disbursements. Those who govern and pacify the prefectures and counties will sincerely care for the people as though protecting infants. All the virtues cultivated within their households will be put to use at the Son of Heaven’s court. None will speak fair words while acting contrary to them, like Gun; none will form partisan cliques, like Gonggong. The numerous worthy officers, assembled in dignity, will be able to broaden their virtuous purposes. They will be much like the four seasons and the five phases, each exercising its capacities to accomplish the transforming work of Heaven’s Way in preserving harmony; the mountains, rivers, and seas…

title: 嘉靖三十八年進士登科錄
text:
各著其功以成坤厚含弘之德
聖明在上夫固不勞而理者也尚何用人理財之
不得其當而久安長治之休不自此而臻也
哉至此則我
皇上體
天之心因臣以慰而諸臣輔理之責亦有感而成
矣
君臣道合相得益章唐虞太和之盛臣何幸親見
之哉臣草茅不識忌諱干冒
天威不勝戰慄之至臣謹對
banxin: 弘治十八年進士登科錄□

矣

punctuated:
各著其功，以成坤厚含弘之德。聖明在上，夫固不勞而理者也。尚何用人理財之不得其當，而久安長治之休不自此而臻也哉？至此，則我皇上體天之心因臣以慰，而諸臣輔理之責亦有感而成矣。君臣道合，相得益章，唐虞太和之盛，臣何幸親見之哉！
臣草茅，不識忌諱，干冒天威，不勝戰慄之至。臣謹對。
translation_en:
…each manifesting its contribution to realize Earth’s virtue of generous support and all-embracing breadth. With a sage and enlightened sovereign above, order assuredly prevails without his exertion. How, then, could the employment of men and management of wealth fail to be appropriate, or the blessings of enduring peace and lasting order fail to follow from this? At this point, Your Majesty’s heart, which takes Heaven as its model, will find comfort through your ministers, while the ministers, moved in response, will fulfill their responsibility to assist in governing. Sovereign and ministers will accord in the Way, each enhancing the other’s distinction. How fortunate your servant would be to witness in person the flourishing supreme harmony of Tang and Yu, the ages of Yao and Shun!
Your servant is a man of the rustic wilds, ignorant of what must be avoided in speech. Having presumed to offend Your Majesty’s awe-inspiring authority, I tremble with fear beyond measure. Your servant respectfully submits this reply.
